[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#1300-1302)#### pub fn [components](https://docs.rs#method.components)(&self) -> [Utf8Components](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Components.html)<'_> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#1300-1302)

#### pub fn [components](https://docs.rs#method.components)(&self) -> [Utf8Components](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Components.html)<'_> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

Produces an iterator over the [ Utf8Component](https://docs.rs/enum.Utf8Component.html)s of the path.

When parsing the path, there is a small amount of normalization:

-
Repeated separators are ignored, so `a/b`and`a//b`both have`a`and`b`as components.
-
Occurrences of `.`are normalized away, except if they are at the beginning of the path. For example,`a/./b`,`a/b/`,`a/b/.`and`a/b`all have`a`and`b`as components, but`./a/b`starts with an additional`CurDir`
-
A trailing slash is normalized away, `/a/b`and`/a/b/`are equivalent.

Note that no other normalization takes place; in particular, `a/c`
and `a/b/../c` are distinct, to account for the possibility that `b`
is a symbolic link (so its parent isn’t `a`).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-35)Examples

```
use camino::{Utf8Component, Utf8Path};
let mut components = Utf8Path::new("/tmp/foo.txt").components();
assert_eq!(components.next(), Some(Utf8Component::RootDir));
assert_eq!(components.next(), Some(Utf8Component::Normal("tmp")));
assert_eq!(components.next(), Some(Utf8Component::Normal("foo.txt")));
assert_eq!(components.next(), None)
```
Produces an iterator over the path’s components viewed as [ str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)
slices.

For more information about the particulars of how the path is separated
into components, see [ components](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.components).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-36)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
let mut it = Utf8Path::new("/tmp/foo.txt").iter();
assert_eq!(it.next(), Some(std::path::MAIN_SEPARATOR.to_string().as_str()));
assert_eq!(it.next(), Some("tmp"));
assert_eq!(it.next(), Some("foo.txt"));
assert_eq!(it.next(), None)
```

`read_link`[§](https://docs.rs#errors-2)Errors

The I/O operation may return an error: see the [ fs::read_link](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/fn.read_link.html)
documentation for more.

If the resulting path is not UTF-8, an [ io::Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/error/struct.Error.html) is returned with the

[set to](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/io/error/enum.ErrorKind.html)

`ErrorKind`[and the payload set to a](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/io/error/enum.ErrorKind.html#variant.InvalidData)

`InvalidData`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.FromPathBufError.html)

`FromPathBufError`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-42)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
let path = Utf8Path::new("/laputa/sky_castle.rs");
let path_link = path.read_link_utf8().expect("read_link call failed");
```
Returns an iterator over the entries within a directory.

The iterator will yield instances of `io::Result``<``fs::DirEntry``>`. New
errors may be encountered after an iterator is initially constructed.

This is an alias to [ fs::read_dir](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/fn.read_dir.html).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-43)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
let path = Utf8Path::new("/laputa");
for entry in path.read_dir().expect("read_dir call failed") {
    if let Ok(entry) = entry {
        println!("{:?}", entry.path());
    }
}
```

Returns `true` if the path points at an existing entity.

Warning: this method may be error-prone, consider using [ try_exists()](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.try_exists) instead!
It also has a risk of introducing time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) bugs.

This function will traverse symbolic links to query information about the
destination file. In case of broken symbolic links this will return `false`.

If you cannot access the directory containing the file, e.g., because of a
permission error, this will return `false`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-45)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert!(!Utf8Path::new("does_not_exist.txt").exists());
```
[§](https://docs.rs#see-also)See Also

This is a convenience function that coerces errors to false. If you want to
check errors, call [ fs::metadata](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/fn.metadata.html).

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#1581-1587)#### pub fn [try_exists](https://docs.rs#method.try_exists)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/error/type.Result.html)<[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#1581-1587)

#### pub fn [try_exists](https://docs.rs#method.try_exists)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/error/type.Result.html)<[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)>

Returns `Ok(true)` if the path points at an existing entity.

This function will traverse symbolic links to query information about the
destination file. In case of broken symbolic links this will return `Ok(false)`.

As opposed to the [ exists()](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.exists) method, this one doesn’t silently ignore errors
unrelated to the path not existing. (E.g. it will return

[in case of permission denied on some of the parent directories.)](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Err)

`Err`Note that while this avoids some pitfalls of the `exists()` method, it still can not
prevent time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) bugs. You should only use it in scenarios
where those bugs are not an issue.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-46)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert!(
    !Utf8Path::new("does_not_exist.txt")
        .try_exists()
        .expect("Can't check existence of file does_not_exist.txt")
);
assert!(Utf8Path::new("/root/secret_file.txt").try_exists().is_err());
```
Returns `true` if the path exists on disk and is pointing at a regular file.

This function will traverse symbolic links to query information about the
destination file. In case of broken symbolic links this will return `false`.

If you cannot access the directory containing the file, e.g., because of a
permission error, this will return `false`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-47)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert_eq!(Utf8Path::new("./is_a_directory/").is_file(), false);
assert_eq!(Utf8Path::new("a_file.txt").is_file(), true);
```

`proptest1`The [ Arbitrary](https://docs.rs/proptest/1.11.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/proptest/arbitrary/traits/trait.Arbitrary.html) impl for

`Utf8PathBuf` returns a path with between 0 and 8 components,
joined by the [for the platform. (Each component is randomly generated, and may itself contain one or more separators.)](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/constant.MAIN_SEPARATOR.html)

`MAIN_SEPARATOR`On Unix, this generates an absolute path half of the time and a relative path the other half.

On Windows, this implementation doesn’t currently generate
[ Utf8PrefixComponent](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PrefixComponent.html) instances, though in the future it might.

# Utf8Path in camino - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/camino/^1.0.5/struct.Utf8Path.html

`pub struct Utf8Path(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

A slice of a UTF-8 path (akin to [ str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)).

This type supports a number of operations for inspecting a path, including
breaking the path into its components (separated by `/` on Unix and by either
`/` or `\` on Windows), extracting the file name, determining whether the path
is absolute, and so on.

This is an *unsized* type, meaning that it must always be used behind a
pointer like `&` or [ Box](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html). For an owned version of this type,
see

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html)

`Utf8PathBuf`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
// Note: this example does work on Windows
let path = Utf8Path::new("./foo/bar.txt");
let parent = path.parent();
assert_eq!(parent, Some(Utf8Path::new("./foo")));
let file_stem = path.file_stem();
assert_eq!(file_stem, Some("bar"));
let extension = path.extension();
assert_eq!(extension, Some("txt"));
```
## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

Directly wraps a string slice as a [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html) slice.

This is a cost-free conversion.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
Utf8Path::new("foo.txt");
```
You can create [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html)s from

[s, or even other](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)

`String`[s:](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html)

`Utf8Path````
use camino::Utf8Path;
let string = String::from("foo.txt");
let from_string = Utf8Path::new(&string);
let from_path = Utf8Path::new(&from_string);
assert_eq!(from_string, from_path);
```
Converts a [ Path](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.Path.html) to a

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html)

`Utf8Path`Returns [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if the path is not valid UTF-8.

For a version that returns a type that implements [ std::error::Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/error/trait.Error.html),
see

[.](https://docs.rs#impl-TryFrom%3C%26Path%3E-for-%26Utf8Path)

`TryFrom<&Path>`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-2)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
use std::ffi::OsStr;
use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
use std::path::Path;
let unicode_path = Path::new("/valid/unicode");
Utf8Path::from_path(unicode_path).expect("valid Unicode path succeeded");
// Paths on Unix can be non-UTF-8.
let non_unicode_str = OsStr::from_bytes(b"\xFF\xFF\xFF");
let non_unicode_path = Path::new(non_unicode_str);
assert!(Utf8Path::from_path(non_unicode_path).is_none(), "non-Unicode path failed");
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#854-856)#### pub fn [is_absolute](https://docs.rs#method.is_absolute)(&self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#854-856)

#### pub fn [is_absolute](https://docs.rs#method.is_absolute)(&self) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Returns `true` if the [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html) is absolute, i.e., if it is independent of
the current directory.

-
On Unix, a path is absolute if it starts with the root, so `is_absolute`and`has_root`
-
On Windows, a path is absolute if it has a prefix and starts with the root: `C:\windows`is absolute, while`C:temp`and`\temp`are not.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-8)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert!(!Utf8Path::new("foo.txt").is_absolute());
```
Returns `true` if the [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html) has a root.

-
On Unix, a path has a root if it begins with `/`.
-
On Windows, a path has a root if it: - has no prefix and begins with a separator, e.g., `\windows`
- has a prefix followed by a separator, e.g., `C:\windows`but not`C:windows`
- has any non-disk prefix, e.g., `\\server\share`

- has no prefix and begins with a separator, e.g.,

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-10)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert!(Utf8Path::new("/etc/passwd").has_root());
```
Returns the [ Path](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.Path.html) without its final component, if there is one.

Returns [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if the path terminates in a root or prefix.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-11)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
let path = Utf8Path::new("/foo/bar");
let parent = path.parent().unwrap();
assert_eq!(parent, Utf8Path::new("/foo"));
let grand_parent = parent.parent().unwrap();
assert_eq!(grand_parent, Utf8Path::new("/"));
assert_eq!(grand_parent.parent(), None);
```
[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#954-956)#### pub fn [ancestors](https://docs.rs#method.ancestors)(&self) -> [Utf8Ancestors](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Ancestors.html)<'_> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#954-956)

#### pub fn [ancestors](https://docs.rs#method.ancestors)(&self) -> [Utf8Ancestors](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Ancestors.html)<'_> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

Produces an iterator over [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html) and its ancestors.

The iterator will yield the [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html) that is returned if the

[method is used zero or more times. That means, the iterator will yield](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.parent)

`parent``&self`, `&self.parent().unwrap()`,
`&self.parent().unwrap().parent().unwrap()` and so on. If the [method returns](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.parent)

`parent`[, the iterator will do likewise. The iterator will always yield at least one value, namely](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None)

`None``&self`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-12)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
let mut ancestors = Utf8Path::new("/foo/bar").ancestors();
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("/foo/bar")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("/foo")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("/")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), None);
let mut ancestors = Utf8Path::new("../foo/bar").ancestors();
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("../foo/bar")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("../foo")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("..")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), Some(Utf8Path::new("")));
assert_eq!(ancestors.next(), None);
```
Returns the final component of the [ Utf8Path](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html), if there is one.

If the path is a normal file, this is the file name. If it’s the path of a directory, this is the directory name.

Returns [ None](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html#variant.None) if the path terminates in

`..`.[§](https://docs.rs#examples-13)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert_eq!(Some("bin"), Utf8Path::new("/usr/bin/").file_name());
assert_eq!(Some("foo.txt"), Utf8Path::new("tmp/foo.txt").file_name());
assert_eq!(Some("foo.txt"), Utf8Path::new("foo.txt/.").file_name());
assert_eq!(Some("foo.txt"), Utf8Path::new("foo.txt/.//").file_name());
assert_eq!(None, Utf8Path::new("foo.txt/..").file_name());
assert_eq!(None, Utf8Path::new("/").file_name());
```

#### pub fn [strip_prefix](https://docs.rs#method.strip_prefix)(
    &self,

Returns a path that, when joined onto `base`, yields `self`.

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

If `base` is not a prefix of `self` (i.e., [ starts_with](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.starts_with)
returns

`false`), returns [.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Err)

`Err`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-14)Examples

```
use camino::{Utf8Path, Utf8PathBuf};
let path = Utf8Path::new("/test/haha/foo.txt");
assert_eq!(path.strip_prefix("/"), Ok(Utf8Path::new("test/haha/foo.txt")));
assert_eq!(path.strip_prefix("/test"), Ok(Utf8Path::new("haha/foo.txt")));
assert_eq!(path.strip_prefix("/test/"), Ok(Utf8Path::new("haha/foo.txt")));
assert_eq!(path.strip_prefix("/test/haha/foo.txt"), Ok(Utf8Path::new("")));
assert_eq!(path.strip_prefix("/test/haha/foo.txt/"), Ok(Utf8Path::new("")));
assert!(path.strip_prefix("test").is_err());
assert!(path.strip_prefix("/haha").is_err());
let prefix = Utf8PathBuf::from("/test/");
assert_eq!(path.strip_prefix(prefix), Ok(Utf8Path::new("haha/foo.txt")));
```

#### pub fn [starts_with](https://docs.rs#method.starts_with)(&self, base: impl [AsRef](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.AsRef.html)<[Path](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.Path.html)>) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Determines whether `base` is a prefix of `self`.

Only considers whole path components to match.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-15)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
let path = Utf8Path::new("/etc/passwd");
assert!(path.starts_with("/etc"));
assert!(path.starts_with("/etc/"));
assert!(path.starts_with("/etc/passwd"));
assert!(path.starts_with("/etc/passwd/")); // extra slash is okay
assert!(path.starts_with("/etc/passwd///")); // multiple extra slashes are okay
assert!(!path.starts_with("/e"));
assert!(!path.starts_with("/etc/passwd.txt"));
assert!(!Utf8Path::new("/etc/foo.rs").starts_with("/etc/foo"));
```
Determines whether `child` is a suffix of `self`.

Only considers whole path components to match.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-16)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
let path = Utf8Path::new("/etc/resolv.conf");
assert!(path.ends_with("resolv.conf"));
assert!(path.ends_with("etc/resolv.conf"));
assert!(path.ends_with("/etc/resolv.conf"));
assert!(!path.ends_with("/resolv.conf"));
assert!(!path.ends_with("conf")); // use .extension() instead
```
Extracts the stem (non-extension) portion of [ self.file_name](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.file_name).

The stem is:

- `None`
- The entire file name if there is no embedded `.`;
- The entire file name if the file name begins with `.`and has no other`.`s within;
- Otherwise, the portion of the file name before the final `.`

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-17)Examples

```

assert_eq!("foo", Utf8Path::new("foo.rs").file_stem().unwrap());
assert_eq!("foo.tar", Utf8Path::new("foo.tar.gz").file_stem().unwrap());

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#1300-1302)#### pub fn [components](https://docs.rs#method.components)(&self) -> [Utf8Components](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Components.html)<'_> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#1300-1302)

#### pub fn [components](https://docs.rs#method.components)(&self) -> [Utf8Components](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Components.html)<'_> [ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

Produces an iterator over the [ Utf8Component](https://docs.rs/enum.Utf8Component.html)s of the path.

When parsing the path, there is a small amount of normalization:

-
Repeated separators are ignored, so `a/b`and`a//b`both have`a`and`b`as components.
-
Occurrences of `.`are normalized away, except if they are at the beginning of the path. For example,`a/./b`,`a/b/`,`a/b/.`and`a/b`all have`a`and`b`as components, but`./a/b`starts with an additional`CurDir`
-
A trailing slash is normalized away, `/a/b`and`/a/b/`are equivalent.

Note that no other normalization takes place; in particular, `a/c`
and `a/b/../c` are distinct, to account for the possibility that `b`
is a symbolic link (so its parent isn’t `a`).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-25)Examples

```
use camino::{Utf8Component, Utf8Path};
let mut components = Utf8Path::new("/tmp/foo.txt").components();
assert_eq!(components.next(), Some(Utf8Component::RootDir));
assert_eq!(components.next(), Some(Utf8Component::Normal("tmp")));
assert_eq!(components.next(), Some(Utf8Component::Normal("foo.txt")));
assert_eq!(components.next(), None)
```
Produces an iterator over the path’s components viewed as [ str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)
slices.

For more information about the particulars of how the path is separated
into components, see [ components](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.components).

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-26)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
let mut it = Utf8Path::new("/tmp/foo.txt").iter();
assert_eq!(it.next(), Some(std::path::MAIN_SEPARATOR.to_string().as_str()));
assert_eq!(it.next(), Some("tmp"));
assert_eq!(it.next(), Some("foo.txt"));
assert_eq!(it.next(), None)
```

Returns `true` if the path points at an existing entity.

Warning: this method may be error-prone, consider using [ try_exists()](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.try_exists) instead!
It also has a risk of introducing time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) bugs.

This function will traverse symbolic links to query information about the
destination file. In case of broken symbolic links this will return `false`.

If you cannot access the directory containing the file, e.g., because of a
permission error, this will return `false`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-35)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert!(!Utf8Path::new("does_not_exist.txt").exists());
```
[§](https://docs.rs#see-also)See Also

This is a convenience function that coerces errors to false. If you want to
check errors, call [ fs::metadata](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/fn.metadata.html).

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#1581-1587)#### pub fn [try_exists](https://docs.rs#method.try_exists)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/error/type.Result.html)<[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#1581-1587)

#### pub fn [try_exists](https://docs.rs#method.try_exists)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/error/type.Result.html)<[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)>

Returns `Ok(true)` if the path points at an existing entity.

This function will traverse symbolic links to query information about the
destination file. In case of broken symbolic links this will return `Ok(false)`.

As opposed to the [ exists()](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.exists) method, this one doesn’t silently ignore errors
unrelated to the path not existing. (E.g. it will return

[in case of permission denied on some of the parent directories.)](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Err)

`Err`Note that while this avoids some pitfalls of the `exists()` method, it still can not
prevent time-of-check to time-of-use (TOCTOU) bugs. You should only use it in scenarios
where those bugs are not an issue.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-36)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert!(
    !Utf8Path::new("does_not_exist.txt")
        .try_exists()
        .expect("Can't check existence of file does_not_exist.txt")
);
assert!(Utf8Path::new("/root/secret_file.txt").try_exists().is_err());
```
Returns `true` if the path exists on disk and is pointing at a regular file.

This function will traverse symbolic links to query information about the
destination file. In case of broken symbolic links this will return `false`.

If you cannot access the directory containing the file, e.g., because of a
permission error, this will return `false`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-37)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert_eq!(Utf8Path::new("./is_a_directory/").is_file(), false);
assert_eq!(Utf8Path::new("a_file.txt").is_file(), true);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#see-also-1)See Also

This is a convenience function that coerces errors to false. If you want to
check errors, call [ fs::metadata](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/fn.metadata.html) and handle its

[. Then call](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)

`Result`[if it was](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/struct.Metadata.html#method.is_file)

`fs::Metadata::is_file`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Ok)

`Ok`When the goal is simply to read from (or write to) the source, the most
reliable way to test the source can be read (or written to) is to open
it. Only using `is_file` can break workflows like `diff <( prog_a )` on
a Unix-like system for example. See [ fs::File::open](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/struct.File.html#method.open) or

[for more information.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/struct.OpenOptions.html#method.open)

`fs::OpenOptions::open`Returns `true` if the path exists on disk and is pointing at a directory.

This function will traverse symbolic links to query information about the
destination file. In case of broken symbolic links this will return `false`.

If you cannot access the directory containing the file, e.g., because of a
permission error, this will return `false`.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-38)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
assert_eq!(Utf8Path::new("./is_a_directory/").is_dir(), true);
assert_eq!(Utf8Path::new("a_file.txt").is_dir(), false);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#see-also-2)See Also

This is a convenience function that coerces errors to false. If you want to
check errors, call [ fs::metadata](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/fn.metadata.html) and handle its

[. Then call](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)

`Result`[if it was](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/struct.Metadata.html#method.is_dir)

`fs::Metadata::is_dir`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Ok)

`Ok`Returns `true` if the path exists on disk and is pointing at a symbolic link.

This function will not traverse symbolic links. In case of a broken symbolic link this will also return true.

If you cannot access the directory containing the file, e.g., because of a permission error, this will return false.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-39)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
use std::os::unix::fs::symlink;
let link_path = Utf8Path::new("link");
symlink("/origin_does_not_exist/", link_path).unwrap();
assert_eq!(link_path.is_symlink(), true);
assert_eq!(link_path.exists(), false);
```
[§](https://docs.rs#see-also-3)See Also

This is a convenience function that coerces errors to false. If you want to
check errors, call [ Utf8Path::symlink_metadata](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.symlink_metadata) and handle its

[. Then call](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)

`Result`[if it was](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/struct.Metadata.html#method.is_symlink)

`fs::Metadata::is_symlink`[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html#variant.Ok)

`Ok`Converts a [ Box<Utf8Path>](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html) into a

[without copying or allocating.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)

`Box<Path>`This is equivalent to the `From<Box<Utf8Path>> for Box<Path>` implementation,
but may aid in type inference.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-40)Examples

```
use camino::{Utf8Path, Utf8PathBuf};
use std::path::Path;
let utf8_path_buf = Utf8PathBuf::from("foo.txt");
let boxed_utf8_path = utf8_path_buf.into_boxed_path();
let boxed_std_path = boxed_utf8_path.into_std_boxed_path();
assert_eq!(boxed_std_path.to_str(), Some("foo.txt"));
// Convert back to a Box<Utf8Path>.
let new_boxed_utf8_path = Utf8Path::from_boxed_path(boxed_std_path).unwrap();
assert_eq!(&*new_boxed_utf8_path, Utf8Path::new("foo.txt"));
```
Creates a new [ Box<Utf8Path>](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html) from a

[containing valid UTF-8 characters, without copying or allocating.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)

`Box<Path>`Errors with the original [ Box<Path>](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html) if it is not valid UTF-8.

For a version that returns a type that implements [ std::error::Error](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/error/trait.Error.html),
see

[.](https://docs.rs#impl-TryFrom%3CBox%3CPath%3E%3E-for-Box%3CUtf8Path%3E)

`TryFrom<Box<Path>>`[§](https://docs.rs#examples-41)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
use std::ffi::OsStr;
use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
use std::path::Path;
let unicode_path: Box<Path> = Path::new("/valid/unicode").into();
Utf8Path::from_boxed_path(unicode_path).expect("valid Unicode path succeeded");
// Paths on Unix can be non-UTF-8.
let non_unicode_str = OsStr::from_bytes(b"\xFF\xFF\xFF");
let non_unicode_path: Box<Path> = Path::new(non_unicode_str).into();
Utf8Path::from_boxed_path(non_unicode_path).expect_err("non-Unicode path failed");
```

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/proptest_impls.rs.html#53-60)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-Arbitrary-for-Box%3CUtf8Path%3E)Available on **crate feature **`proptest1` only.The `Arbitrary``Box<Utf8Path>` returns a path with between 0 and 8 components,
joined by the `MAIN_SEPARATOR`

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/proptest_impls.rs.html#53-60)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-Arbitrary-for-Box%3CUtf8Path%3E)

**crate feature**only.

`proptest1`The [ Arbitrary](https://docs.rs/proptest/1.11.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/proptest/arbitrary/traits/trait.Arbitrary.html) impl for

`Box<Utf8Path>` returns a path with between 0 and 8 components,
joined by the [for the platform. (Each component is randomly generated, and may itself contain one or more separators.)](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/constant.MAIN_SEPARATOR.html)

`MAIN_SEPARATOR`On Unix, this generates an absolute path half of the time and a relative path the other half.

On Windows, this implementation doesn’t currently generate
[ Utf8PrefixComponent](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PrefixComponent.html) instances, though in the future it might.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-42)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
use std::convert::TryFrom;
use std::ffi::OsStr;
use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
use std::path::Path;
let non_unicode_str = OsStr::from_bytes(b"\xFF\xFF\xFF");
assert!(<&Utf8Path>::try_from(non_unicode_str).is_err(), "non-Unicode string path failed");
```
Returns [ FromPathError](https://docs.rs/struct.FromPathError.html) if the path is not valid UTF-8.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-43)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
use std::convert::TryFrom;
use std::ffi::OsStr;
use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
use std::path::Path;
let unicode_path = Path::new("/valid/unicode");
<&Utf8Path>::try_from(unicode_path).expect("valid Unicode path succeeded");
// Paths on Unix can be non-UTF-8.
let non_unicode_str = OsStr::from_bytes(b"\xFF\xFF\xFF");
let non_unicode_path = Path::new(non_unicode_str);
assert!(<&Utf8Path>::try_from(non_unicode_path).is_err(), "non-Unicode path failed");
```

# FromBoxedPathError in camino - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/camino/^1.0.5/struct.FromBoxedPathError.html

`pub struct FromBoxedPathError { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A possible error value while converting a [ Box<Path>](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html) to a

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)

`Box<Utf8Path>`Produced by the [ TryFrom<Box<Path>>](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#impl-TryFrom%3CBox%3CPath%3E%3E-for-Box%3CUtf8Path%3E) implementation for

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/boxed/struct.Box.html)

`Box<Utf8Path>`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use camino::{Utf8Path, FromBoxedPathError};
use std::convert::{TryFrom, TryInto};
use std::ffi::OsStr;
use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
use std::path::Path;
let unicode_path: Box<Path> = Path::new("/valid/unicode").into();
let utf8_path: Box<Utf8Path> = unicode_path.try_into().expect("valid Unicode path succeeded");
// Paths on Unix can be non-UTF-8.
let non_unicode_str = OsStr::from_bytes(b"\xFF\xFF\xFF");
let non_unicode_path: Box<Path> = Path::new(non_unicode_str).into();
let err: FromBoxedPathError = <Box<Utf8Path>>::try_from(non_unicode_path.clone())
    .expect_err("non-Unicode path failed");
assert_eq!(err.as_path(), &*non_unicode_path);
assert_eq!(err.into_boxed_path(), non_unicode_path);
```

A possible error value while converting a [ Path](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.Path.html) to a

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html)

`Utf8Path`Produced by the [ TryFrom<&Path>](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#impl-TryFrom%3C%26Path%3E-for-%26Utf8Path) implementation for

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html)

`&Utf8Path`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use camino::{Utf8Path, FromPathError};
use std::convert::{TryFrom, TryInto};
use std::ffi::OsStr;
use std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt;
use std::path::Path;
let unicode_path = Path::new("/valid/unicode");
let utf8_path: &Utf8Path = unicode_path.try_into().expect("valid Unicode path succeeded");
// Paths on Unix can be non-UTF-8.
let non_unicode_str = OsStr::from_bytes(b"\xFF\xFF\xFF");
let non_unicode_path = Path::new(non_unicode_str);
let err: FromPathError = <&Utf8Path>::try_from(non_unicode_path)
    .expect_err("non-Unicode path failed");
```

# Utf8Component in camino - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/camino/^1.0.5/enum.Utf8Component.html

```
pub enum Utf8Component<'a> {
    Prefix(
```
[Utf8PrefixComponent](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PrefixComponent.html)<'a>),
    RootDir,
    CurDir,
    ParentDir,
    Normal(&'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)),
}## Expand description

A single component of a path.

A [ Utf8Component](https://docs.rs/enum.Utf8Component.html) roughly corresponds to a substring between path separators
(

`/` or `\`).This `enum` is created by iterating over [ Utf8Components](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Components.html), which in turn is
created by the

[method on](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.components)

`components`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html)

`Utf8Path`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use camino::{Utf8Component, Utf8Path};
let path = Utf8Path::new("/tmp/foo/bar.txt");
let components = path.components().collect::<Vec<_>>();
assert_eq!(&components, &[
    Utf8Component::RootDir,
    Utf8Component::Normal("tmp"),
    Utf8Component::Normal("foo"),
    Utf8Component::Normal("bar.txt"),
]);
```
## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Prefix)

### Prefix([Utf8PrefixComponent](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PrefixComponent.html)<'a>)

A Windows path prefix, e.g., `C:` or `\\server\share`.

There is a large variety of prefix types, see [ Utf8Prefix](https://docs.rs/enum.Utf8Prefix.html)’s documentation
for more.

Does not occur on Unix.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.RootDir)

### RootDir

The root directory component, appears after any prefix and before anything else.

It represents a separator that designates that a path starts from root.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.CurDir)

### CurDir

A reference to the current directory, i.e., `.`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.ParentDir)

### ParentDir

A reference to the parent directory, i.e., `..`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Normal)

### Normal(&'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html))

A normal component, e.g., `a` and `b` in `a/b`.

This variant is the most common one, it represents references to files or directories.

# Utf8Components in camino - Rust

`pub struct Utf8Components<'a>(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

An iterator over the [ Utf8Component](https://docs.rs/enum.Utf8Component.html)s of a

[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html)

`Utf8Path`This `struct` is created by the [ components](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.components) method on

[. See its documentation for more.](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html)

`Utf8Path`[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
let path = Utf8Path::new("/tmp/foo/bar.txt");
for component in path.components() {
    println!("{:?}", component);
}
```

### impl<'a> [Utf8Components](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Components.html)<'a>

Extracts a slice corresponding to the portion of the path remaining for iteration.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
let mut components = Utf8Path::new("/tmp/foo/bar.txt").components();
components.next();
components.next();
assert_eq!(Utf8Path::new("foo/bar.txt"), components.as_path());
```

# Utf8DirEntry in camino - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/camino/^1.0.5/struct.Utf8DirEntry.html

`pub struct Utf8DirEntry { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

Entries returned by the [ ReadDirUtf8](https://docs.rs/struct.ReadDirUtf8.html) iterator.

An instance of [ Utf8DirEntry](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8DirEntry.html) represents an entry inside of a directory on the filesystem. Each
entry can be inspected via methods to learn about the full path or possibly other metadata.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#2424-2575)[§](https://docs.rs#impl-Utf8DirEntry)### impl [Utf8DirEntry](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8DirEntry.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/camino/lib.rs.html#2424-2575)

[§](https://docs.rs#impl-Utf8DirEntry)

### impl [Utf8DirEntry](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8DirEntry.html)

Returns the full path to the file that this entry represents.

The full path is created by joining the original path to `read_dir`
with the filename of this entry.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
fn main() -> std::io::Result<()> {
    for entry in Utf8Path::new(".").read_dir_utf8()? {
        let dir = entry?;
        println!("{}", dir.path());
    }
    Ok(())
}
```
This prints output like:

```
./whatever.txt
./foo.html
./hello_world.rs
```
The exact text, of course, depends on what files you have in `.`.

Returns the metadata for the file that this entry points at.

This function will not traverse symlinks if this entry points at a symlink. To traverse
symlinks use [ Utf8Path::metadata](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.metadata) or

[.](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/fs/struct.File.html#method.metadata)

`fs::File::metadata`[§](https://docs.rs#platform-specific-behavior)Platform-specific behavior

On Windows this function is cheap to call (no extra system calls
needed), but on Unix platforms this function is the equivalent of
calling `symlink_metadata` on the path.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-1)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
if let Ok(entries) = Utf8Path::new(".").read_dir_utf8() {
    for entry in entries {
        if let Ok(entry) = entry {
            // Here, `entry` is a `Utf8DirEntry`.
            if let Ok(metadata) = entry.metadata() {
                // Now let's show our entry's permissions!
                println!("{}: {:?}", entry.path(), metadata.permissions());
            } else {
                println!("Couldn't get metadata for {}", entry.path());
            }
        }
    }
}
```
Returns the file type for the file that this entry points at.

This function will not traverse symlinks if this entry points at a symlink.

[§](https://docs.rs#platform-specific-behavior-1)Platform-specific behavior

On Windows and most Unix platforms this function is free (no extra
system calls needed), but some Unix platforms may require the equivalent
call to `symlink_metadata` to learn about the target file type.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-2)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
if let Ok(entries) = Utf8Path::new(".").read_dir_utf8() {
    for entry in entries {
        if let Ok(entry) = entry {
            // Here, `entry` is a `DirEntry`.
            if let Ok(file_type) = entry.file_type() {
                // Now let's show our entry's file type!
                println!("{}: {:?}", entry.path(), file_type);
            } else {
                println!("Couldn't get file type for {}", entry.path());
            }
        }
    }
}
```
Returns the bare file name of this directory entry without any other leading path component.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples-3)Examples

```
use camino::Utf8Path;
if let Ok(entries) = Utf8Path::new(".").read_dir_utf8() {
    for entry in entries {
        if let Ok(entry) = entry {
            // Here, `entry` is a `DirEntry`.
            println!("{}", entry.file_name());
        }
    }
}
```

# Utf8PrefixComponent in camino - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/camino/^1.0.5/struct.Utf8PrefixComponent.html

`pub struct Utf8PrefixComponent<'a>(/* private fields */);`## Expand description

A structure wrapping a Windows path prefix as well as its unparsed string representation.

In addition to the parsed [ Utf8Prefix](https://docs.rs/enum.Utf8Prefix.html) information returned by

[,](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PrefixComponent.html#method.kind)

`kind`[also holds the raw and unparsed](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PrefixComponent.html)

`Utf8PrefixComponent`[slice, returned by](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)

`str`[.](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PrefixComponent.html#method.as_str)

`as_str`Instances of this `struct` can be obtained by matching against the
[ Prefix variant](https://docs.rs/enum.Utf8Component.html#variant.Prefix) on

[.](https://docs.rs/enum.Utf8Component.html)

`Utf8Component`Does not occur on Unix.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use camino::{Utf8Component, Utf8Path, Utf8Prefix};
use std::ffi::OsStr;
let path = Utf8Path::new(r"C:\you\later\");
match path.components().next().unwrap() {
    Utf8Component::Prefix(prefix_component) => {
        assert_eq!(Utf8Prefix::Disk(b'C'), prefix_component.kind());
        assert_eq!("C:", prefix_component.as_str());
    }
    _ => unreachable!(),
}
```

# Utf8Prefix in camino - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/camino/^1.0.5/enum.Utf8Prefix.html

```
pub enum Utf8Prefix<'a> {
    Verbatim(&'a
```
[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)),
    VerbatimUNC(&'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html), &'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)),
    VerbatimDisk([u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)),
    DeviceNS(&'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)),
    UNC(&'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html), &'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)),
    Disk([u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)),
}## Expand description

Windows path prefixes, e.g., `C:` or `\\server\share`.

Windows uses a variety of path prefix styles, including references to drive
volumes (like `C:`), network shared folders (like `\\server\share`), and
others. In addition, some path prefixes are “verbatim” (i.e., prefixed with
`\\?\`), in which case `/` is *not* treated as a separator and essentially
no normalization is performed.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

```
use camino::{Utf8Component, Utf8Path, Utf8Prefix};
use camino::Utf8Prefix::*;
fn get_path_prefix(s: &str) -> Utf8Prefix {
    let path = Utf8Path::new(s);
    match path.components().next().unwrap() {
        Utf8Component::Prefix(prefix_component) => prefix_component.kind(),
        _ => panic!(),
    }
}
assert_eq!(Verbatim("pictures"), get_path_prefix(r"\\?\pictures\kittens"));
assert_eq!(VerbatimUNC("server", "share"), get_path_prefix(r"\\?\UNC\server\share"));
assert_eq!(VerbatimDisk(b'C'), get_path_prefix(r"\\?\C:\"));
assert_eq!(DeviceNS("BrainInterface"), get_path_prefix(r"\\.\BrainInterface"));
assert_eq!(UNC("server", "share"), get_path_prefix(r"\\server\share"));
assert_eq!(Disk(b'C'), get_path_prefix(r"C:\Users\Rust\Pictures\Ferris"));
```
## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Verbatim)

### Verbatim(&'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html))

Verbatim prefix, e.g., `\\?\cat_pics`.

Verbatim prefixes consist of `\\?\` immediately followed by the given
component.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.VerbatimUNC)

Verbatim prefix using Windows’ * Uniform Naming Convention*,
e.g.,

`\\?\UNC\server\share`.Verbatim UNC prefixes consist of `\\?\UNC\` immediately followed by the
server’s hostname and a share name.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.VerbatimDisk)

### VerbatimDisk([u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html))

Verbatim disk prefix, e.g., `\\?\C:`.

Verbatim disk prefixes consist of `\\?\` immediately followed by the
drive letter and `:`.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.DeviceNS)

### DeviceNS(&'a [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html))

Device namespace prefix, e.g., `\\.\COM42`.

Device namespace prefixes consist of `\\.\` immediately followed by the
device name.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.UNC)

Prefix using Windows’ * Uniform Naming Convention*, e.g.

`\\server\share`.UNC prefixes consist of the server’s hostname and a share name.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Disk)

### Disk([u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html))

Prefix `C:` for the given disk drive.

# absolute_utf8 in camino - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/camino/^1.0.5/fn.absolute_utf8.html

`pub fn absolute_utf8<P: `[AsRef](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/convert/trait.AsRef.html)<[Path](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/path/struct.Path.html)>>(path: P) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/error/type.Result.html)<[Utf8PathBuf](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html)>**only.**

`absolute_path`## Expand description

Makes the path absolute without accessing the filesystem, converting it to a [ Utf8PathBuf](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8PathBuf.html).

If the path is relative, the current directory is used as the base directory. All intermediate
components will be resolved according to platform-specific rules, but unlike
[ canonicalize](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.canonicalize) or

[, this does not resolve symlinks and may succeed even if the path does not exist.](https://docs.rs/struct.Utf8Path.html#method.canonicalize_utf8)

`canonicalize_utf8`*Requires Rust 1.79 or newer.*

[§](https://docs.rs#errors)Errors

Errors if:

- The path is empty.
- The [current directory](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/env/fn.current_dir.html)cannot be determined.
- The path is not valid UTF-8.

[§](https://docs.rs#examples)Examples

[§](https://docs.rs#posix-paths)POSIX paths

```
fn main() -> std::io::Result<()> {
    use camino::Utf8Path;
    // Relative to absolute
    let absolute = camino::absolute_utf8("foo/./bar")?;
    assert!(absolute.ends_with("foo/bar"));
    // Absolute to absolute
    let absolute = camino::absolute_utf8("/foo//test/.././bar.rs")?;
    assert_eq!(absolute, Utf8Path::new("/foo/test/../bar.rs"));
    Ok(())
}
```
The path is resolved using [POSIX semantics](https://pubs.opengroup.org/onlinepubs/9699919799/basedefs/V1_chap04.html#tag_04_13) except that it stops short of
resolving symlinks. This means it will keep `..` components and trailing slashes.

[§](https://docs.rs#windows-paths)Windows paths

```
fn main() -> std::io::Result<()> {
    use camino::Utf8Path;
    // Relative to absolute
    let absolute = camino::absolute_utf8("foo/./bar")?;
    assert!(absolute.ends_with(r"foo\bar"));
    // Absolute to absolute
    let absolute = camino::absolute_utf8(r"C:\foo//test\..\./bar.rs")?;
    assert_eq!(absolute, Utf8Path::new(r"C:\foo\bar.rs"));
    Ok(())
}
```
For verbatim paths this will simply return the path as given. For other paths this is currently
equivalent to calling [ GetFullPathNameW](https://docs.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/fileapi/nf-fileapi-getfullpathnamew).

Note that this [may change in the future](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/io/index.html#platform-specific-behavior).

# cfg_if - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/cfg-if/1.0.4/target-redirect/cfg_if/

## Expand description

A macro for defining `#[cfg]` if-else statements.

The macro provided by this crate, `cfg_if`, is similar to the `if/elif` C
preprocessor macro by allowing definition of a cascade of `#[cfg]` cases,
emitting the implementation which matches first.

This allows you to conveniently provide a long list `#[cfg]`’d blocks of code
without having to rewrite each clause multiple times.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

```
cfg_if::cfg_if! {
    if #[cfg(unix)] {
        fn foo() { /* unix specific functionality */ }
    } else if #[cfg(target_pointer_width = "32")] {
        fn foo() { /* non-unix, 32-bit functionality */ }
    } else {
        fn foo() { /* fallback implementation */ }
    }
}
```
## Macros[§](https://docs.rs#macros)

- [cfg_if](https://docs.rs/macro.cfg_if.html)
- The main macro provided by this crate. See crate documentation for more information.

        )*
        $(
            else { $( $e_tokens:tt )* }
        )?
    ) => { ... };
    (@__items ( $( ($($_:tt)*) , )* ) ; ) => { ... };
    (
        @__items ( $( ($($no:tt)+) , )* ) ;
        (( $( $($yes:tt)+ )? ) ( $( $tokens:tt )* )),
        $( $rest:tt , )*
    ) => { ... };

[42](https://docs.rs#42)/// ```
[43](https://docs.rs#43)pub fn diff_paths<P, B>(path: P, base: B) -> Option<PathBuf>
[44](https://docs.rs#44)where
[45](https://docs.rs#45)    P: AsRef<Path>,
[46](https://docs.rs#46)    B: AsRef<Path>,
[47](https://docs.rs#47){
[48](https://docs.rs#48)    let path = path.as_ref();
[49](https://docs.rs#49)    let base = base.as_ref();
[50](https://docs.rs#50)
[51](https://docs.rs#51)    if path.is_absolute() != base.is_absolute() {
[52](https://docs.rs#52)        if path.is_absolute() {
[53](https://docs.rs#53)            Some(PathBuf::from(path))
[54](https://docs.rs#54)        } else {
[55](https://docs.rs#55)            None
[56](https://docs.rs#56)        }
[57](https://docs.rs#57)    } else {
[58](https://docs.rs#58)        let mut ita = path.components();
[59](https://docs.rs#59)        let mut itb = base.components();
[60](https://docs.rs#60)        let mut comps: Vec<Component> = vec![];
[61](https://docs.rs#61)        loop {
[62](https://docs.rs#62)            match (ita.next(), itb.next()) {
[63](https://docs.rs#63)                (None, None) => break,
[64](https://docs.rs#64)                (Some(a), None) => {
[65](https://docs.rs#65)                    comps.push(a);
[66](https://docs.rs#66)                    comps.extend(ita.by_ref());
[67](https://docs.rs#67)                    break;
[68](https://docs.rs#68)                }
[69](https://docs.rs#69)                (None, _) => comps.push(Component::ParentDir),
[70](https://docs.rs#70)                (Some(a), Some(b)) if comps.is_empty() && a == b => (),
[71](https://docs.rs#71)                (Some(a), Some(b)) if b == Component::CurDir => comps.push(a),
[72](https://docs.rs#72)                (Some(_), Some(b)) if b == Component::ParentDir => return None,
[73](https://docs.rs#73)                (Some(a), Some(_)) => {
[74](https://docs.rs#74)                    comps.push(Component::ParentDir);
[75](https://docs.rs#75)                    for _ in itb {
[76](https://docs.rs#76)                        comps.push(Component::ParentDir);
[77](https://docs.rs#77)                    }
[78](https://docs.rs#78)                    comps.push(a);
[79](https://docs.rs#79)                    comps.extend(ita.by_ref());
[80](https://docs.rs#80)                    break;
[81](https://docs.rs#81)                }
[82](https://docs.rs#82)            }
[83](https://docs.rs#83)        }
[84](https://docs.rs#84)        Some(comps.iter().map(|c| c.as_os_str()).collect())
[85](https://docs.rs#85)    }
[86](https://docs.rs#86)}
[87](https://docs.rs#87)
[88](https://docs.rs#88)#[cfg(feature = "camino")]
[89](https://docs.rs#89)mod utf8_paths {
[90](https://docs.rs#90)    use camino::{Utf8Component, Utf8Path, Utf8PathBuf};
[91](https://docs.rs#91)
[92](https://docs.rs#92)    /// Construct a relative UTF-8 path from a provided base directory path to the provided path.
[93](https://docs.rs#93)    ///
[94](https://docs.rs#94)    /// Requires the `camino` feature.
[95](https://docs.rs#95)    ///
[96](https://docs.rs#96)    /// ```rust
[97](https://docs.rs#97)    /// # extern crate camino;
[98](https://docs.rs#98)    /// use camino::*;
[99](https://docs.rs#99)    /// use pathdiff::diff_utf8_paths;
[100](https://docs.rs#100)    ///
[101](https://docs.rs#101)    /// assert_eq!(diff_utf8_paths("/foo/bar",      "/foo/bar/baz"),  Some("../".into()));
[102](https://docs.rs#102)    /// assert_eq!(diff_utf8_paths("/foo/bar/baz",  "/foo/bar"),      Some("baz".into()));
[103](https://docs.rs#103)    /// assert_eq!(diff_utf8_paths("/foo/bar/quux", "/foo/bar/baz"),  Some("../quux".into()));
[104](https://docs.rs#104)    /// assert_eq!(diff_utf8_paths("/foo/bar/baz",  "/foo/bar/quux"), Some("../baz".into()));
[105](https://docs.rs#105)    /// assert_eq!(diff_utf8_paths("/foo/bar",      "/foo/bar/quux"), Some("../".into()));
[106](https://docs.rs#106)    ///
[107](https://docs.rs#107)    /// assert_eq!(diff_utf8_paths("/foo/bar",      "baz"),           Some("/foo/bar".into()));
[108](https://docs.rs#108)    /// assert_eq!(diff_utf8_paths("/foo/bar",      "/baz"),          Some("../foo/bar".into()));
[109](https://docs.rs#109)    /// assert_eq!(diff_utf8_paths("foo",           "bar"),           Some("../foo".into()));
[110](https://docs.rs#110)    ///
[111](https://docs.rs#111)    /// assert_eq!(
[112](https://docs.rs#112)    ///     diff_utf8_paths(&"/foo/bar/baz", "/foo/bar".to_string()),
[113](https://docs.rs#113)    ///     Some("baz".into())
[114](https://docs.rs#114)    /// );
[115](https://docs.rs#115)    /// assert_eq!(
[116](https://docs.rs#116)    ///     diff_utf8_paths(Utf8Path::new("/foo/bar/baz"), Utf8Path::new("/foo/bar").to_path_buf()),
[117](https://docs.rs#117)    ///     Some("baz".into())
[118](https://docs.rs#118)    /// );
[119](https://docs.rs#119)    /// ```
[120](https://docs.rs#120)    #[cfg_attr(docsrs, doc(cfg(feature = "camino")))]
[121](https://docs.rs#121)    pub fn diff_utf8_paths<P, B>(path: P, base: B) -> Option<Utf8PathBuf>
[122](https://docs.rs#122)    where
[123](https://docs.rs#123)        P: AsRef<Utf8Path>,
[124](https://docs.rs#124)        B: AsRef<Utf8Path>,
[125](https://docs.rs#125)    {
[126](https://docs.rs#126)        let path = path.as_ref();
[127](https://docs.rs#127)        let base = base.as_ref();
[128](https://docs.rs#128)
[129](https://docs.rs#129)        if path.is_absolute() != base.is_absolute() {
[130](https://docs.rs#130)            if path.is_absolute() {
[131](https://docs.rs#131)                Some(Utf8PathBuf::from(path))
[132](https://docs.rs#132)            } else {
[133](https://docs.rs#133)                None
[134](https://docs.rs#134)            }
[135](https://docs.rs#135)        } else {
[136](https://docs.rs#136)            let mut ita = path.components();
[137](https://docs.rs#137)            let mut itb = base.components();
[138](https://docs.rs#138)            let mut comps: Vec<Utf8Component> = vec![];
[139](https://docs.rs#139)            loop {
[140](https://docs.rs#140)                match (ita.next(), itb.next()) {
[141](https://docs.rs#141)                    (None, None) => break,
[142](https://docs.rs#142)                    (Some(a), None) => {
[143](https://docs.rs#143)                        comps.push(a);
[144](https://docs.rs#144)                        comps.extend(ita.by_ref());
[145](https://docs.rs#145)                        break;
[146](https://docs.rs#146)                    }
[147](https://docs.rs#147)                    (None, _) => comps.push(Utf8Component::ParentDir),
[148](https://docs.rs#148)                    (Some(a), Some(b)) if comps.is_empty() && a == b => (),
[149](https://docs.rs#149)                    (Some(a), Some(b)) if b == Utf8Component::CurDir => comps.push(a),
[150](https://docs.rs#150)                    (Some(_), Some(b)) if b == Utf8Component::ParentDir => return None,
[151](https://docs.rs#151)                    (Some(a), Some(_)) => {
[152](https://docs.rs#152)                        comps.push(Utf8Component::ParentDir);
[153](https://docs.rs#153)                        for _ in itb {
[154](https://docs.rs#154)                            comps.push(Utf8Component::ParentDir);
[155](https://docs.rs#155)                        }
[156](https://docs.rs#156)                        comps.push(a);
[157](https://docs.rs#157)                        comps.extend(ita.by_ref());
[158](https://docs.rs#158)                        break;
[159](https://docs.rs#159)                    }
[160](https://docs.rs#160)                }
[161](https://docs.rs#161)            }
[162](https://docs.rs#162)            Some(comps.iter().map(|c| c.as_str()).collect())
[163](https://docs.rs#163)        }
[164](https://docs.rs#164)    }
[165](https://docs.rs#165)}

# diff_paths in pathdiff - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/pathdiff/latest/target-redirect/pathdiff/fn.diff_paths.html

## Expand description

Construct a relative path from a provided base directory path to the provided path.

```
use pathdiff::diff_paths;
use std::path::*;
assert_eq!(diff_paths("/foo/bar",      "/foo/bar/baz"),  Some("../".into()));
assert_eq!(diff_paths("/foo/bar/baz",  "/foo/bar"),      Some("baz".into()));
assert_eq!(diff_paths("/foo/bar/quux", "/foo/bar/baz"),  Some("../quux".into()));
assert_eq!(diff_paths("/foo/bar/baz",  "/foo/bar/quux"), Some("../baz".into()));
assert_eq!(diff_paths("/foo/bar",      "/foo/bar/quux"), Some("../".into()));
assert_eq!(diff_paths("/foo/bar",      "baz"),           Some("/foo/bar".into()));
assert_eq!(diff_paths("/foo/bar",      "/baz"),          Some("../foo/bar".into()));
assert_eq!(diff_paths("foo",           "bar"),           Some("../foo".into()));
assert_eq!(
    diff_paths(&"/foo/bar/baz", "/foo/bar".to_string()),
    Some("baz".into())
);
assert_eq!(
    diff_paths(Path::new("/foo/bar/baz"), Path::new("/foo/bar").to_path_buf()),
    Some("baz".into())
);
```

# clap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/clap

## Expand description

Command Line Argument Parser for Rust

Quick Links:

- Derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)
- Builder [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_tutorial/index.html)and[reference](https://docs.rs/struct.Command.html)
- [Cookbook](https://docs.rs/_cookbook/index.html)
- [CLI Concepts](https://docs.rs/_concepts/index.html)
- [FAQ](https://docs.rs/_faq/index.html)
- [Discussions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/discussions)
- [CHANGELOG](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/blob/v4.6.1/CHANGELOG.md)(includes major version migration guides)

[§](https://docs.rs#aspirations)Aspirations

- Out of the box, users get a polished CLI experience
- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output, [shell completions](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/tree/master/clap_complete), etc

- Including common argument behavior, help generation, suggested fixes for users, colored output,
- Flexible enough to port your existing CLI interface
- However, we won’t necessarily streamline support for each use case

- Reasonable parse performance
- Resilient maintainership, including
- Willing to break compatibility rather than batching up breaking changes in large releases
- Leverage feature flags to keep to one active branch
- Being under [WG-CLI](https://github.com/rust-cli/team/)to increase the bus factor

- We follow semver and will wait about 6-9 months between major breaking changes
- We will support the last two minor Rust releases (MSRV, currently 1.74)

While these aspirations can be at odds with fast build times and low binary
size, we will still strive to keep these reasonable for the flexibility you
get.  Check out the
[argparse-benchmarks](https://github.com/rust-cli/argparse-benchmarks-rs) for
CLI parsers optimized for other use cases.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Run

`$ cargo add clap --features derive`*(See also  feature flag reference)*

Then define your CLI in `main.rs`:

```
use clap::Parser;
/// Simple program to greet a person
#[derive(Parser, Debug)]
#[command(version, about, long_about = None)]
struct Args {
    /// Name of the person to greet
    #[arg(short, long)]
    name: String,
    /// Number of times to greet
    #[arg(short, long, default_value_t = 1)]
    count: u8,
}
fn main() {
    let args = Args::parse();
    for _ in 0..args.count {
        println!("Hello {}!", args.name);
    }
}
```
And try it out:

```
$ demo --help
A simple to use, efficient, and full-featured Command Line Argument Parser
Usage: demo[EXE] [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>
Options:
  -n, --name <NAME>    Name of the person to greet
  -c, --count <COUNT>  Number of times to greet [default: 1]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
$ demo --name Me
Hello Me!
```
*(version number and  .exe extension on windows replaced by placeholders)*

See also the derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html) and [reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)

[§](https://docs.rs#related-projects)Related Projects

Augment clap:

- [wild](https://crates.io/crates/wild)for supporting wildcards (- `*`) on Windows like you do Linux
- [argfile](https://crates.io/crates/argfile)for loading additional arguments from a file (aka response files)
- [shadow-rs](https://crates.io/crates/shadow-rs)for generating- `Command::long_version`
- [clap_mangen](https://crates.io/crates/clap_mangen)for generating man page source (roff)
- [clap_complete](https://crates.io/crates/clap_complete)for shell completion support
- [clap-i18n-richformatter](https://crates.io/crates/clap-i18n-richformatter)for i18n support with- `clap::error::RichFormatter`

CLI Helpers

- [clio](https://crates.io/crates/clio)for reading/writing to files specified as arguments
- [clap-verbosity-flag](https://crates.io/crates/clap-verbosity-flag)
- [clap-cargo](https://crates.io/crates/clap-cargo)
- [colorchoice-clap](https://crates.io/crates/colorchoice-clap)

Testing

- `trycmd`
- `snapbox`
- `assert_cmd`- `assert_fs`

- Willing to break compatibility rather than batching up breaking changes in large releases
- Leverage feature flags to keep to one active branch
- Being under [WG-CLI](https://github.com/rust-cli/team/)to increase the bus factor

- We follow semver and will wait about 6-9 months between major breaking changes
- We will support the last two minor Rust releases (MSRV, currently 1.74)

While these aspirations can be at odds with fast build times and low binary
size, we will still strive to keep these reasonable for the flexibility you
get.  Check out the
[argparse-benchmarks](https://github.com/rust-cli/argparse-benchmarks-rs) for
CLI parsers optimized for other use cases.

[§](https://docs.rs#example)Example

Run

`$ cargo add clap --features derive`*(See also  feature flag reference)*

Then define your CLI in `main.rs`:

```
use clap::Parser;
/// Simple program to greet a person
#[derive(Parser, Debug)]
#[command(version, about, long_about = None)]
struct Args {
    /// Name of the person to greet
    #[arg(short, long)]
    name: String,
    /// Number of times to greet
    #[arg(short, long, default_value_t = 1)]
    count: u8,
}
fn main() {
    let args = Args::parse();
    for _ in 0..args.count {
        println!("Hello {}!", args.name);
    }
}
```
And try it out:

```
$ demo --help
A simple to use, efficient, and full-featured Command Line Argument Parser
Usage: demo[EXE] [OPTIONS] --name <NAME>
Options:
  -n, --name <NAME>    Name of the person to greet
  -c, --count <COUNT>  Number of times to greet [default: 1]
  -h, --help           Print help
  -V, --version        Print version
$ demo --name Me
Hello Me!
```
*(version number and  .exe extension on windows replaced by placeholders)*

See also the derive [tutorial](https://docs.rs/_derive/_tutorial/index.html) and [reference](https://docs.rs/_derive/index.html)

# clap - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/clap/%7E2

## Expand description

`clap` is a simple-to-use, efficient, and full-featured library for parsing command line
arguments and subcommands when writing console/terminal applications.

`clap` is used to parse *and validate* the string of command line arguments provided by the user
at runtime. You provide the list of valid possibilities, and `clap` handles the rest. This means
you focus on your *applications* functionality, and less on the parsing and validating of
arguments.

`clap` also provides the traditional version and help switches (or flags) ‘for free’ meaning
automatically with no configuration. It does this by checking the list of valid possibilities you
supplied and adding only the ones you haven’t already defined. If you are using subcommands,
`clap` will also auto-generate a `help` subcommand for you in addition to the traditional flags.

Once `clap` parses the user provided string of arguments, it returns the matches along with any
applicable values. If the user made an error or typo, `clap` informs them of the mistake and
exits gracefully (or returns a `Result` type and allows you to perform any clean up prior to
exit). Because of this, you can make reasonable assumptions in your code about the validity of
the arguments.

The following examples show a quick example of some of the very basic functionality of `clap`.
For more advanced usage, such as requirements, conflicts, groups, multiple values and
occurrences see the [documentation](https://docs.rs/clap/), [examples/](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/tree/v2.34.0/examples) directory of
this repository or the [video tutorials](https://www.youtube.com/playlist?list=PLza5oFLQGTl2Z5T8g1pRkIynR3E0_pc7U).

**NOTE:** All of these examples are functionally the same, but show different styles in which to
use `clap`

The first example shows a method that allows more advanced configuration options (not shown in this small example), or even dynamically generating arguments when desired. The downside is it’s more verbose.

```
// (Full example with detailed comments in examples/01b_quick_example.rs)
//
// This example demonstrates clap's full 'builder pattern' style of creating arguments which is
// more verbose, but allows easier editing, and at times more advanced options, or the possibility
// to generate arguments dynamically.
extern crate clap;
use clap::{Arg, App, SubCommand};
fn main() {
    let matches = App::new("My Super Program")
                          .version("1.0")
                          .author("Kevin K. <kbknapp@gmail.com>")
                          .about("Does awesome things")
                          .arg(Arg::with_name("config")
                               .short("c")
                               .long("config")
                               .value_name("FILE")
                               .help("Sets a custom config file")
                               .takes_value(true))
                          .arg(Arg::with_name("INPUT")
                               .help("Sets the input file to use")
                               .required(true)
                               .index(1))
                          .arg(Arg::with_name("v")
                               .short("v")
                               .multiple(true)
                               .help("Sets the level of verbosity"))
                          .subcommand(SubCommand::with_name("test")
                                      .about("controls testing features")
                                      .version("1.3")
                                      .author("Someone E. <someone_else@other.com>")
                                      .arg(Arg::with_name("debug")
                                          .short("d")
                                          .help("print debug information verbosely")))
                          .get_matches();
    // Gets a value for config if supplied by user, or defaults to "default.conf"
    let config = matches.value_of("config").unwrap_or("default.conf");
    println!("Value for config: {}", config);
    // Calling .unwrap() is safe here because "INPUT" is required (if "INPUT" wasn't
    // required we could have used an 'if let' to conditionally get the value)
    println!("Using input file: {}", matches.value_of("INPUT").unwrap());
    // Vary the output based on how many times the user used the "verbose" flag
    // (i.e. 'myprog -v -v -v' or 'myprog -vvv' vs 'myprog -v'
    match matches.occurrences_of("v") {
        0 => println!("No verbose info"),
        1 => println!("Some verbose info"),
        2 => println!("Tons of verbose info"),
        3 | _ => println!("Don't be crazy"),
    }
    // You can handle information about subcommands by requesting their matches by name
    // (as below), requesting just the name used, or both at the same time
    if let Some(matches) = matches.subcommand_matches("test") {
        if matches.is_present("debug") {
            println!("Printing debug info...");
        } else {
            println!("Printing normally...");
        }
    }
    // more program logic goes here...
}
```
The next example shows a far less verbose method, but sacrifices some of the advanced
configuration options (not shown in this small example). This method also takes a *very* minor
runtime penalty.

```
// (Full example with detailed comments in examples/01a_quick_example.rs)
//
// This example demonstrates clap's "usage strings" method of creating arguments
// which is less verbose
extern crate clap;
use clap::{Arg, App, SubCommand};
fn main() {
    let matches = App::new("myapp")
                          .version("1.0")
                          .author("Kevin K. <kbknapp@gmail.com>")
                          .about("Does awesome things")
                          .args_from_usage(
                              "-c, --config=[FILE] 'Sets a custom config file'
                              <INPUT>              'Sets the input file to use'
                              -v...                'Sets the level of verbosity'")
                          .subcommand(SubCommand::with_name("test")
                                      .about("controls testing features")
                                      .version("1.3")
                                      .author("Someone E. <someone_else@other.com>")
                                      .arg_from_usage("-d, --debug 'Print debug information'"))
                          .get_matches();
    // Same as previous example...
}
```
This third method shows how you can use a YAML file to build your CLI and keep your Rust source tidy or support multiple localized translations by having different YAML files for each localization.

First, create the `cli.yml` file to hold your CLI options, but it could be called anything we
like:

```
name: myapp
version: "1.0"
author: Kevin K. <kbknapp@gmail.com>
about: Does awesome things
args:
    - config:
        short: c
        long: config
        value_name: FILE
        help: Sets a custom config file
        takes_value: true
    - INPUT:
        help: Sets the input file to use
        required: true
        index: 1
    - verbose:
        short: v
        multiple: true
        help: Sets the level of verbosity
subcommands:
    - test:
        about: controls testing features
        version: "1.3"
        author: Someone E. <someone_else@other.com>
        args:
            - debug:
                short: d
                help: print debug information
```
Since this feature requires additional dependencies that not everyone may want, it is *not*
compiled in by default and we need to enable a feature flag in Cargo.toml:

Simply change your `clap = "~2.27.0"` to `clap = {version = "~2.27.0", features = ["yaml"]}`.

At last we create our `main.rs` file just like we would have with the previous two examples:

[ⓘ](https://docs.rs)

```
// (Full example with detailed comments in examples/17_yaml.rs)
//
// This example demonstrates clap's building from YAML style of creating arguments which is far
// more clean, but takes a very small performance hit compared to the other two methods.
#[macro_use]
extern crate clap;
use clap::App;
fn main() {
    // The YAML file is found relative to the current file, similar to how modules are found
    let yaml = load_yaml!("cli.yml");
    let matches = App::from_yaml(yaml).get_matches();
    // Same as previous examples...
}
```
Finally there is a macro version, which is like a hybrid approach offering the speed of the builder pattern (the first example), but without all the verbosity.

```
#[macro_use]
extern crate clap;
fn main() {
    let matches = clap_app!(myapp =>
        (version: "1.0")
        (author: "Kevin K. <kbknapp@gmail.com>")
        (about: "Does awesome things")
        (@arg CONFIG: -c --config +takes_value "Sets a custom config file")
        (@arg INPUT: +required "Sets the input file to use")
        (@arg debug: -d ... "Sets the level of debugging information")
        (@subcommand test =>
            (about: "controls testing features")
            (version: "1.3")
            (author: "Someone E. <someone_else@other.com>")
            (@arg verbose: -v --verbose "Print test information verbosely")
        )
    ).get_matches();
    // Same as before...
}
```
If you were to compile any of the above programs and run them with the flag `--help` or `-h` (or
`help` subcommand, since we defined `test` as a subcommand) the following would be output

```
$ myprog --help
My Super Program 1.0
Kevin K. <kbknapp@gmail.com>
Does awesome things
USAGE:
    MyApp [FLAGS] [OPTIONS] <INPUT> [SUBCOMMAND]
FLAGS:
    -h, --help       Prints this message
    -v               Sets the level of verbosity
    -V, --version    Prints version information
OPTIONS:
    -c, --config <FILE>    Sets a custom config file
ARGS:
    INPUT    The input file to use
SUBCOMMANDS:
    help    Prints this message
    test    Controls testing features
```
**NOTE:** You could also run `myapp test --help` to see similar output and options for the
`test` subcommand.

- `suggestions`: Turns on the- `Did you mean '--myoption'?`feature for when users make typos. (builds dependency- `strsim`)
- `color`: Turns on colored error messages. This feature only works on non-Windows OSs. (builds dependency- `ansi-term`and- `atty`)
- `wrap_help`: Wraps the help at the actual terminal width when available, instead of 120 characters. (builds dependency- `textwrap`with feature- `term_size`)

To disable these, add this to your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[dependencies.clap]
version = "~2.27.0"
default-features = false
```
You can also selectively enable only the features you’d like to include, by adding:

```
[dependencies.clap]
version = "~2.27.0"
default-features = false
# Cherry-pick the features you'd like to use
features = [ "suggestions", "color" ]
```
- **“yaml”**: Enables building CLIs from YAML documents. (builds dependency- `yaml-rust`)
- **“unstable”**: Enables unstable- `clap`features that may change from release to release

There are a few goals of `clap` that I’d like to maintain throughout contributions. If your
proposed changes break, or go against any of these goals we’ll discuss the changes further
before merging (but will *not* be ignored, all contributes are welcome!). These are by no means
hard-and-fast rules, as I’m no expert and break them myself from time to time (even if by
mistake or ignorance).

- Remain backwards compatible when possible
- If backwards compatibility *must*be broken, use deprecation warnings if at all possible before removing legacy code - This does not apply for security concerns

- If backwards compatibility
- Parse arguments quickly
- Parsing of arguments shouldn’t slow down usage of the main program - This is also true of
generating help and usage information (although *slightly*less stringent, as the program is about to exit)

- Parsing of arguments shouldn’t slow down usage of the main program - This is also true of
generating help and usage information (although
- Try to be cognizant of memory usage
- Once parsing is complete, the memory footprint of `clap`should be low since the main program is the star of the show

- Once parsing is complete, the memory footprint of
- `panic!`on- *developer*error, exit gracefully on- *end-user*error

Because `clap` takes `SemVer` and compatibility seriously, this is the official policy regarding
breaking changes and previous versions of Rust.

`clap` will pin the minimum required version of Rust to the CI builds. Bumping the minimum
version of Rust is considered a minor breaking change, meaning *at a minimum* the minor version
of `clap` will be bumped.

In order to keep from being surprised by breaking changes, it is **highly** recommended to use
the `~major.minor.patch` style in your `Cargo.toml`:

```
[dependencies] clap = "~2.27.0"
```
This will cause *only* the patch version to be updated upon a `cargo update` call, and therefore
cannot break due to new features, or bumped minimum versions of Rust.

`clap` will officially support current stable Rust, minus two releases, but may work with prior
releases as well. For example, current stable Rust at the time of this writing is 1.21.0,
meaning `clap` is guaranteed to compile with 1.19.0 and beyond. At the 1.22.0 release, `clap`
will be guaranteed to compile with 1.20.0 and beyond, etc.

Upon bumping the minimum version of Rust (assuming it’s within the stable-2 range), it *must* be
clearly annotated in the `CHANGELOG.md`

`clap` is licensed under the MIT license. Please read the [LICENSE-MIT](https://github.com/clap-rs/clap/blob/v2.34.0/LICENSE-MIT) file in
this repository for more information.
