# kigumi_db - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/crate/kigumi-db/0.1.0/target-redirect/kigumi_db/

## Expand description

Postgres persistence layer.

Closes the loop: the metamodel’s generated DDL creates real tables, and a [ Domain](https://docs.rs/kigumi-core/0.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/kigumi_core/domain/enum.Domain.html) is
compiled to a PARAMETERIZED

`WHERE` whose values are BOUND (never interpolated) before
execution. The `*_secured` methods enforce the security engine (ACL + record rules) at the
database boundary: access is checked, and the user’s record-rule domain is AND-ed into the
query — so a user can never read rows the rules forbid.## Structs[§](https://docs.rs#structs)

- [AclRow](https://docs.rs/struct.AclRow.html)
- One configured ACL row (for listing/inspection).
- [Cron](https://docs.rs/struct.CronRegistration.html)- Registration
- Registration of a scheduled job (emitted by hand or a future `register_cron!`).
- [Custom](https://docs.rs/struct.CustomField.html)- Field
- A runtime-defined field. Strings are owned (they come from the DB, not the compile-time `'static`catalog); the host leaks them when it builds a`FieldDef`.
- [Data](https://docs.rs/struct.DataMigrationRegistration.html)- Migration - Registration
- [Db](https://docs.rs/struct.Db.html)
- A connection pool to a Postgres database. `Clone`shares the same pool (cheap;`PgPool`is an`Arc`internally) — e.g. to hand a handle to the background cron scheduler.
- [JobRegistration](https://docs.rs/struct.JobRegistration.html)
- Registration of a job kind, emitted by `register_job!`.`max_attempts`counts executions, not retries: 1 = never retry; the webhook-parity default in the macro is 8.
- [Ledger](https://docs.rs/struct.LedgerReportRegistration.html)- Report - Registration
- Registration of a report by name, emitted by `register_report!`.`read_model`is the model whose Read ACL gates it (e.g. account.account);`groups`(if non-empty) further restricts who may run it.
- [List](https://docs.rs/struct.ListPage.html)- Page
- A page of list results plus the total count under the same secured domain.
- [Migration](https://docs.rs/struct.Migration.html)
- One migration step: the SQL that brings a module’s schema/data up to `version`.
- [Outbox](https://docs.rs/struct.OutboxEvent.html)- Event
- A domain event to enqueue. `change_summary`is small JSON metadata (changed fields, a deleted row’s last snapshot, a state transition) — never the full record, which the dispatcher reads fresh at delivery so a webhook always reflects committed truth.
- [Outgoing](https://docs.rs/struct.OutgoingMail.html)- Mail
- One queued outgoing email handed to the host’s SMTP transport by `Db::flush_outgoing_mail`
- [Route](https://docs.rs/struct.RouteInput.html)- Input
- Everything a module route body receives, expressed in DB/JSON terms (no axum types):
the caller context (authenticated, or the GUEST context for `auth: false`routes), the query params, the parsed JSON body (empty when the body is not a JSON object — NOT an error: webhook senders post forms and raw payloads), the EXACT raw bytes (HMAC signature verification must hash what was sent, not a re-serialization), and the request headers (lowercased names, duplicate values joined with “, “).
- [Route](https://docs.rs/struct.RouteRegistration.html)- Registration
- Registration of a module HTTP route, emitted by `register_route!`. Keyed by (name, method) — a provider like Meta uses GET for its verification handshake and POST for delivery on the SAME path.`auth: true`routes require a bearer (plus the optional group gate);`auth: false`routes run under the GUEST context — uid −1, NO groups, non-su — which the default-deny ACL engine blocks from every secured read/write, so the body must authenticate the caller itself (e.g. an HMAC signature over`raw_body`) and then elevate explicitly via`Ctx::sudo`(the same greppable idiom as`ServiceCtx::elevated`).
- [RuleRow](https://docs.rs/struct.RuleRow.html)
- One configured DB record rule (for listing/inspection).
- [Seed](https://docs.rs/struct.SeedRegistration.html)- Registration
- [Service](https://docs.rs/struct.ServiceCtx.html)- Ctx
- The secured-primitive surface handed to a service body. A concrete struct (no trait, no `dyn`): its methods are`async fn`s delegating to`Db`’s secured CRUD under the caller’s context, so the security engine is re-applied on every call. The ERP model-name literals a body resolves live in the MODULE, never in this crate.
- [Service](https://docs.rs/struct.ServiceInput.html)- Input
- The route `:id`plus the POST JSON body (e.g. a payment`{amount, journal_id}`).
- [Service](https://docs.rs/struct.ServiceOutput.html)- Output
- What a service returns: free-form JSON the handler relays verbatim (services produce a result — an id,
a count, a report — not a same-record diff like an `ActionOutcome`).
- [Service](https://docs.rs/struct.ServiceRegistration.html)- Registration
- Registration of a service by (model, name) — the transactional twin of `ActionRegistration`.`write_gate`selects the ACL operation the dispatcher checks (Write for a mutating service, Read for a read-only one such as a report).`groups`(if non-empty) restricts who may run it, on top of the ACL.
- [Stored](https://docs.rs/struct.StoredEvent.html)- Event
- One outbox row as the live event stream reads it — the SSE counterpart of the webhook envelope.
- [UserRow](https://docs.rs/struct.UserRow.html)
- A user row used for credential verification.
- [View](https://docs.rs/struct.ViewOverride.html)- Override
- A runtime UI override for one field. `label`/`widget`replace the contract value when set;`invisible`drops the field from the served contract;`readonly`locks it;`invisible_when`/`readonly_when`carry a JSON domain AST for conditional visibility/lock. All fields are data — none reaches DDL.
- [Webhook](https://docs.rs/struct.WebhookDelivery.html)- Delivery
- A claimed delivery handed to the host’s HTTP transport. `payload["id"]`(evt_) is the stable idempotency key across retries; `attempts`is the count BEFORE this attempt.
- [Write](https://docs.rs/struct.WriteTriggerRegistration.html)- Trigger - Registration
- Registration of a write trigger, emitted by `register_write_trigger!`.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [DbError](https://docs.rs/enum.DbError.html)
- [Migration](https://docs.rs/enum.MigrationOutcome.html)- Outcome
- [Route](https://docs.rs/enum.RouteMethod.html)- Method
- HTTP method of a module route. An enum here (not an http-crate type) keeps this crate HTTP-free; the server translates. Get also serves HEAD (axum’s default).
- [Route](https://docs.rs/enum.RouteOutput.html)- Output
- What a module route returns: JSON (the normal case) or PLAIN TEXT — some webhook providers’ challenge handshakes require echoing a token as an unquoted text body (a JSON string would be quoted and fail their exact-match).

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_safe_ident.html)- safe_ - ident
- A Postgres identifier safe to interpolate into DDL: lowercase start, then letters/digits/underscore.
Custom-field names and the model table are validated against this before any `ALTER TABLE`.
- [job_for](https://docs.rs/fn.job_for.html)
- Looks up a registered job kind.
- [ledger_](https://docs.rs/fn.ledger_report_for.html)- report_ - for
- Looks up a registered report by name.
- [ledger_](https://docs.rs/fn.ledger_report_names.html)- report_ - names
- All registered report names (for a UI report menu).
- [m2m_](https://docs.rs/fn.m2m_junction_ddl.html)- junction_ - ddl
- Builds the SELECT column list for a model. NUMERIC columns are cast to float8 so they decode
into `f64`without a decimal dependency. Identifiers come from the model, never user input. Registered models that have a One2many field targeting`child_model_name`, paired with the inverse FK column — i.e. the aggregate parents to recompute when such a child changes. The exact junction-table DDL for a model’s Many2many fields — the single source shared by`Db::create_m2m_relations`
- [registered_](https://docs.rs/fn.registered_crons.html)- crons
- All compile-time-registered cron jobs.
- [route_](https://docs.rs/fn.route_for.html)- for
- Looks up a route by (name, method).
- [route_](https://docs.rs/fn.route_methods.html)- methods
- The methods registered under `name`(for the 405 Allow header when the method doesn’t match).
- [service_](https://docs.rs/fn.service_for.html)- for
- Looks up a registered service by model + name.
- [services_](https://docs.rs/fn.services_for.html)- for
- All services registered on `model`(for the UI contract, so a form can render its service buttons).
- [validate_](https://docs.rs/fn.validate_routes.html)- routes
- Startup validation of the route registry: names must be single path segments (the generic
`/api/x/:route`route can’t match a slash) and (name, method) must be unique. Call once when building the router; a violation is an authoring bug, not a runtime condition.
- [write_](https://docs.rs/fn.write_triggers_for.html)- triggers_ - for
- The write triggers registered on `model`(empty when none — the common case, iterated per secured write).

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [BoxService](https://docs.rs/type.BoxServiceFut.html)- Fut
- A boxed Send future borrowing the `&mut ServiceCtx`for lifetime`'c`— what lets a service body`.await`secured-CRUD calls while holding the context borrow.
- [CronFn](https://docs.rs/type.CronFn.html)
- A scheduled job’s body. The returned future borrows `db`for the duration of the run.
- [Data](https://docs.rs/type.DataMigrationFn.html)- Migration - Fn
- A versioned per-module DATA migration (emitted by `register_migration!`): the upgrade contract. Runs when migrate finds the module installed at a ledger version <`to_version`while the linked crate is >=`to_version`. Steps run in semver order, each bumping the ledger to its`to_version`— a failed upgrade resumes exactly where it stopped, so bodies must be idempotent (at-least-once, like jobs). A fresh install runs no migrations: the declarative schema is already current-shape, and the ledger starts at the linked version.
- [JobFn](https://docs.rs/type.JobFn.html)
- A registered job body: owns its payload, reaches the DB through the full handle (same trust
class as a cron body). Return `Err`to schedule a retry (or dead-letter past`max_attempts`).
- [Ledger](https://docs.rs/type.LedgerReportFn.html)- Report - Fn
- A read-only REPORT fn — bespoke aggregate SQL over the pool returning JSON rows, with optional query params. The read-only, record-less sibling of a service (a report has no record id): gated only on Read of a declared model, then dispatched generically. The ERP report logic lives in the module that owns the tables; the core just gates + dispatches.
- [RouteFn](https://docs.rs/type.RouteFn.html)
- A registered module route body: bespoke logic over the full `Db`handle. Same trust class as a service body (`ServiceCtx::pool`already hands services the raw pool past the gate): module code is trusted first-party code once it compiles; AUTHORIZATION is the dispatcher’s job.
- [SeedFn](https://docs.rs/type.SeedFn.html)
- A module’s reference-data seeder (emitted by `register_seed!`). Runs at EVERY migrate for installed modules, in dependency order — so bodies must be idempotent and never overwrite an operator change (guard with count/exists checks: the DB is the authority).
- [Service](https://docs.rs/type.ServiceFn.html)- Fn
- A registered service fn. A HRTB plain `fn`pointer (so it is storable in`inventory`, like`ActionFn`) returning a boxed future whose lifetime is tied to the`&mut ServiceCtx`borrow. Module authors write a bare`async fn(&mut ServiceCtx, ServiceInput) -> Result<ServiceOutput, DbError>`and`register_service!`wraps it with the one`Box::pin`.
- [Write](https://docs.rs/type.WriteTriggerFn.html)- Trigger - Fn
- An in-tx WRITE TRIGGER — a module hook that runs on the caller’s transaction AFTER a secured write to
`model`, when one of`watch`ed columns changed (empty = any). The framework’s own`depends`-driven recompute handles same-record + child aggregates; this seam covers the effects it can’t express on read — chiefly a Many2many aggregate stored across a join (e.g. a product variant’s`price_extra`summed over its attribute-value cells). Runs on`&mut Transaction`only (no ACL re-entry), so it stays a pure, engine-owned in-tx side effect, atomic with the write. ZERO ERP literals reach this crate — the model name and the SQL live in the module that owns the tables.

## Enums[§](https://docs.rs#enums)

- [DbError](https://docs.rs/enum.DbError.html)
- [Migration](https://docs.rs/enum.MigrationOutcome.html)- Outcome
- [Route](https://docs.rs/enum.RouteMethod.html)- Method
- HTTP method of a module route. An enum here (not an http-crate type) keeps this crate HTTP-free; the server translates. Get also serves HEAD (axum’s default).
- [Route](https://docs.rs/enum.RouteOutput.html)- Output
- What a module route returns: JSON (the normal case) or PLAIN TEXT — some webhook providers’ challenge handshakes require echoing a token as an unquoted text body (a JSON string would be quoted and fail their exact-match).

## Functions[§](https://docs.rs#functions)

- [is_](https://docs.rs/fn.is_safe_ident.html)- safe_ - ident
- A Postgres identifier safe to interpolate into DDL: lowercase start, then letters/digits/underscore.
Custom-field names and the model table are validated against this before any `ALTER TABLE`.
- [job_for](https://docs.rs/fn.job_for.html)
- Looks up a registered job kind.
- [ledger_](https://docs.rs/fn.ledger_report_for.html)- report_ - for
- Looks up a registered report by name.
- [ledger_](https://docs.rs/fn.ledger_report_names.html)- report_ - names
- All registered report names (for a UI report menu).
- [m2m_](https://docs.rs/fn.m2m_junction_ddl.html)- junction_ - ddl
- Builds the SELECT column list for a model. NUMERIC columns are cast to float8 so they decode
into `f64`without a decimal dependency. Identifiers come from the model, never user input. Registered models that have a One2many field targeting`child_model_name`, paired with the inverse FK column — i.e. the aggregate parents to recompute when such a child changes. The exact junction-table DDL for a model’s Many2many fields — the single source shared by`Db::create_m2m_relations`
- [registered_](https://docs.rs/fn.registered_crons.html)- crons
- All compile-time-registered cron jobs.
- [route_](https://docs.rs/fn.route_for.html)- for
- Looks up a route by (name, method).
- [route_](https://docs.rs/fn.route_methods.html)- methods
- The methods registered under `name`(for the 405 Allow header when the method doesn’t match).
- [service_](https://docs.rs/fn.service_for.html)- for
- Looks up a registered service by model + name.
- [services_](https://docs.rs/fn.services_for.html)- for
- All services registered on `model`(for the UI contract, so a form can render its service buttons).
- [validate_](https://docs.rs/fn.validate_routes.html)- routes
- Startup validation of the route registry: names must be single path segments (the generic
`/api/x/:route`route can’t match a slash) and (name, method) must be unique. Call once when building the router; a violation is an authoring bug, not a runtime condition.
- [write_](https://docs.rs/fn.write_triggers_for.html)- triggers_ - for
- The write triggers registered on `model`(empty when none — the common case, iterated per secured write).

## Type Aliases[§](https://docs.rs#types)

- [BoxService](https://docs.rs/type.BoxServiceFut.html)- Fut
- A boxed Send future borrowing the `&mut ServiceCtx`for lifetime`'c`— what lets a service body`.await`secured-CRUD calls while holding the context borrow.
- [CronFn](https://docs.rs/type.CronFn.html)
- A scheduled job’s body. The returned future borrows `db`for the duration of the run.
- [Data](https://docs.rs/type.DataMigrationFn.html)- Migration - Fn
- A versioned per-module DATA migration (emitted by `register_migration!`): the upgrade contract. Runs when migrate finds the module installed at a ledger version <`to_version`while the linked crate is >=`to_version`. Steps run in semver order, each bumping the ledger to its`to_version`— a failed upgrade resumes exactly where it stopped, so bodies must be idempotent (at-least-once, like jobs). A fresh install runs no migrations: the declarative schema is already current-shape, and the ledger starts at the linked version.
- [JobFn](https://docs.rs/type.JobFn.html)
- A registered job body: owns its payload, reaches the DB through the full handle (same trust
class as a cron body). Return `Err`to schedule a retry (or dead-letter past`max_attempts`).
- [Ledger](https://docs.rs/type.LedgerReportFn.html)- Report - Fn
- A read-only REPORT fn — bespoke aggregate SQL over the pool returning JSON rows, with optional query params. The read-only, record-less sibling of a service (a report has no record id): gated only on Read of a declared model, then dispatched generically. The ERP report logic lives in the module that owns the tables; the core just gates + dispatches.
- [RouteFn](https://docs.rs/type.RouteFn.html)
- A registered module route body: bespoke logic over the full `Db`handle. Same trust class as a service body (`ServiceCtx::pool`already hands services the raw pool past the gate): module code is trusted first-party code once it compiles; AUTHORIZATION is the dispatcher’s job.
- [SeedFn](https://docs.rs/type.SeedFn.html)
- A module’s reference-data seeder (emitted by `register_seed!`). Runs at EVERY migrate for installed modules, in dependency order — so bodies must be idempotent and never overwrite an operator change (guard with count/exists checks: the DB is the authority).
- [Service](https://docs.rs/type.ServiceFn.html)- Fn
- A registered service fn. A HRTB plain `fn`pointer (so it is storable in`inventory`, like`ActionFn`) returning a boxed future whose lifetime is tied to the`&mut ServiceCtx`borrow. Module authors write a bare`async fn(&mut ServiceCtx, ServiceInput) -> Result<ServiceOutput, DbError>`and`register_service!`wraps it with the one`Box::pin`.
- [Write](https://docs.rs/type.WriteTriggerFn.html)- Trigger - Fn
- An in-tx WRITE TRIGGER — a module hook that runs on the caller’s transaction AFTER a secured write to
`model`, when one of`watch`ed columns changed (empty = any). The framework’s own`depends`-driven recompute handles same-record + child aggregates; this seam covers the effects it can’t express on read — chiefly a Many2many aggregate stored across a join (e.g. a product variant’s`price_extra`summed over its attribute-value cells). Runs on`&mut Transaction`only (no ACL re-entry), so it stays a pure, engine-owned in-tx side effect, atomic with the write. ZERO ERP literals reach this crate — the model name and the SQL live in the module that owns the tables.

[378](#378)                if !check_access(Operation::Read, child.name, ctx, acls) {
[379](#379)                    continue; }
[381](#381)                let cdom = Domain::field(inverse).eq(id);
[382](#382)                let children = self.find_secured(&child, ctx, acls, rules, Some(&cdom)).await?;
[383](#383)                obj.insert(f.name.to_string(), Json::Array(children));
[384](#384)            }
[385](#385)        }
[386](#386)        Ok(Some(Json::Object(obj)))
[387](#387)    }
[388](#388)
[389](#389)    fn secured_read_domain(
[392](#392)        &self,
[393](#393)        model: &ResolvedModel,
[394](#394)        ctx: &Ctx,
[395](#395)        acls: &[Acl],
[396](#396)        rules: &[RecordRule],
[397](#397)        filter: Option<&Domain>,
[398](#398)    ) -> Result<Domain, DbError> {
[399](#399)        if !check_access(Operation::Read, model.name, ctx, acls) {
[400](#400)            return Err(DbError::AccessDenied {
[401](#401)                model: model.name.to_string(),
[402](#402)                operation: "read",
[403](#403)            });
[404](#404)        }
[405](#405)        if let Some(f) = filter {
[410](#410)            for path in f.condition_paths() {
[411](#411)                if !filter_path_accessible(model, path, ctx) {
[412](#412)                    return Err(DbError::AccessDenied {
[413](#413)                        model: model.name.to_string(),
[414](#414)                        operation: "filter (restricted field)",
[415](#415)                    });
[416](#416)                }
[417](#417)            }
[418](#418)        }
[419](#419)        let rule = record_rule_domain(Operation::Read, model.name, ctx, rules);
[420](#420)        let base = match (filter, rule) {
[421](#421)            (Some(f), Some(r)) => f.clone().and(r),
[422](#422)            (Some(f), None) => f.clone(),
[423](#423)            (None, Some(r)) => r,
[424](#424)            (None, None) => Domain::True,
[425](#425)        };
[426](#426)        Ok(match company_filter(model, ctx) {
[428](#428)            Some(cf) => base.and(cf),
[429](#429)            None => base,
[430](#430)        })
[431](#431)    }

[452](#452)    async fn insert_secured_in_tx(
[458](#458)        &self,
[459](#459)        model: &ResolvedModel,
[460](#460)        ctx: &Ctx,
[461](#461)        acls: &[Acl],
[462](#462)        rules: &[RecordRule],
[463](#463)        values: &Map<String, Json>,
[464](#464)        tx: &mut sqlx::Transaction<'_, Postgres>,
[465](#465)    ) -> Result<(i64, BTreeMap<String, Value>), DbError> {
[466](#466)        if !check_access(Operation::Create, model.name, ctx, acls) {
[467](#467)            return Err(DbError::AccessDenied { model: model.name.to_string(), operation: "create" });
[468](#468)        }
[469](#469)        check_writable_fields(model, ctx, values)?; let (mut scalars, nested, m2m, delegated) = split_nested(model, values)?;
[473](#473)
[474](#474)        if let Some((parent, via)) = inherits_of(model.name) {
[479](#479)            let parent_model = resolve_registered(parent).map_err(DbError::BadInput)?;
[480](#480)            let has_via = scalars.get(via).is_some_and(|v| !v.is_null());
[481](#481)            if has_via {
[482](#482)                if !delegated.is_empty() {
[483](#483)                    let pid = scalars.get(via).and_then(|v| v.as_i64()).ok_or_else(|| {
[484](#484)                        DbError::BadInput(format!("_inherits via '{via}' must be an integer id"))
[485](#485)                    })?;
[486](#486)                    self.update_delegated_parent(&parent_model, ctx, acls, rules, pid, &delegated, tx).await?;
[487](#487)                }
[488](#488)            } else {
[489](#489)                if !check_access(Operation::Create, parent_model.name, ctx, acls) {
[490](#490)                    return Err(DbError::AccessDenied {
[491](#491)                        model: parent_model.name.to_string(),
[492](#492)                        operation: "create (inherited parent)",
[493](#493)                    });
[494](#494)                }
[495](#495)                check_writable_fields(&parent_model, ctx, &delegated)?;
[496](#496)                let mut pscalars = delegated.clone();
[497](#497)                let (pid, _) =
[498](#498)                    self.insert_scalars_in_tx(&parent_model, ctx, rules, &mut pscalars, tx).await?;
[499](#499)                scalars.insert(via.to_string(), Json::from(pid));
[500](#500)            }
[501](#501)        }
[502](#502)
[503](#503)        let (id, record) = self.insert_scalars_in_tx(model, ctx, rules, &mut scalars, tx).await?;
[505](#505)
[506](#506)        if !nested.is_empty() {
[511](#511)            self.apply_nested_in_tx(tx, ctx, acls, rules, &nested, id, false).await?;
[512](#512)            recompute_columns_on(tx, model, id).await?;
[513](#513)        }
[514](#514)        if !m2m.is_empty() {
[516](#516)            apply_m2m_in_tx(tx, id, &m2m).await?;
[517](#517)        }
[518](#518)        if has_constraints(model.name) {
[521](#521)            check_constraints_in_tx(model, tx, id, None).await?;
[522](#522)        }
[523](#523)        let company_id = record.get("company_id").and_then(|v| match v {
[525](#525)            Value::Int(n) => Some(*n),
[526](#526)            _ => None,
[527](#527)        });
[528](#528)        self.enqueue_event_in_tx(
[529](#529)            tx,
[530](#530)            &OutboxEvent {
[531](#531)                event_type: "model.created".to_string(),
[532](#532)                model: model.name.to_string(),
[533](#533)                record_id: id,
[534](#534)                author_uid: Some(ctx.uid),
[535](#535)                company_id,
[536](#536)                change_summary: serde_json::json!({}),
[537](#537)            },
[538](#538)        )
[539](#539)        .await?;
[540](#540)        Ok((id, record))
[541](#541)    }
[542](#542)
[543](#543)    async fn insert_scalars_in_tx(
[548](#548)        &self,
[549](#549)        model: &ResolvedModel,
[550](#550)        ctx: &Ctx,
[551](#551)        rules: &[RecordRule],
[552](#552)        scalars: &mut Map<String, Json>,
[553](#553)        tx: &mut sqlx::Transaction<'_, Postgres>,
[554](#554)    ) -> Result<(i64, BTreeMap<String, Value>), DbError> {
[555](#555)        apply_company_scope(model, ctx, scalars, true)?;
[556](#556)        apply_defaults(model, scalars);
[557](#557)        let mut cols = validate_write_values(model, scalars, true)?;
[558](#558)        cols.extend(readonly_default_columns(model, &cols)?);
[561](#561)        if cols.is_empty() {
[562](#562)            return Err(DbError::BadInput("no values provided".to_string()));
[563](#563)        }
[564](#564)        let mut record: BTreeMap<String, Value> =
[565](#565)            cols.into_iter().map(|(c, v)| (c.to_string(), v)).collect();
[566](#566)        compute_stored(model, &mut record, &Children::new());
[567](#567)        let (names, vals): (Vec<&str>, Vec<Value>) =
[568](#568)            record.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.as_str(), v.clone())).unzip();
[569](#569)        let placeholders: Vec<String> =
[570](#570)            names.iter().enumerate().map(|(i, c)| format!("${}::{}", i + 1, col_cast(model, c))).collect();
[571](#571)        let sql = format!(
[572](#572)            "INSERT INTO {} ({}) VALUES ({}) RETURNING id",
[573](#573)            model.table,
[574](#574)            names.join(", "),
[575](#575)            placeholders.join(", ")
[576](#576)        );
[577](#577)        let mut q = sqlx::query_scalar::<Postgres, i64>(&sql);
[578](#578)        q = bind_all(q, &vals);
[579](#579)        let id: i64 = q.fetch_one(&mut **tx).await?;
[580](#580)        if let Some(rule) = record_rule_domain(Operation::Create, model.name, ctx, rules) {
[581](#581)            let mut params: Vec<Value> = vec![Value::Int(id)];
[582](#582)            let where_sql = rule.compile_into(model, &mut params)?;
[583](#583)            let check = format!("SELECT 1 FROM {} WHERE id = $1 AND {}", model.table, where_sql);
[584](#584)            let mut cq = sqlx::query(&check);
[585](#585)            for v in ¶ms {
[586](#586)                cq = bind_query(cq, v);
[587](#587)            }
[588](#588)            if cq.fetch_optional(&mut **tx).await?.is_none() {
[589](#589)                return Err(DbError::AccessDenied {
[590](#590)                    model: model.name.to_string(),
[591](#591)                    operation: "create (record rule)",
[592](#592)                });
[593](#593)            }
[594](#594)        }
[595](#595)        Ok((id, record))
[596](#596)    }
[597](#597)
[598](#598)    #[allow(clippy::too_many_arguments)]
[603](#603)    async fn update_delegated_parent(
[604](#604)        &self,
[605](#605)        parent_model: &ResolvedModel,
[606](#606)        ctx: &Ctx,
[607](#607)        acls: &[Acl],
[608](#608)        rules: &[RecordRule],
[609](#609)        pid: i64,
[610](#610)        delegated: &Map<String, Json>,
[611](#611)        tx: &mut sqlx::Transaction<'_, Postgres>,
[612](#612)    ) -> Result<(), DbError> {
[613](#613)        if !check_access(Operation::Write, parent_model.name, ctx, acls) {
[614](#614)            return Err(DbError::AccessDenied {
[615](#615)                model: parent_model.name.to_string(),
[616](#616)                operation: "write (inherited parent)",
[617](#617)            });
[618](#618)        }
[619](#619)        check_writable_fields(parent_model, ctx, delegated)?; let mut d = delegated.clone();
[621](#621)        apply_company_scope(parent_model, ctx, &mut d, false)?;
[622](#622)        let cols = validate_write_values(parent_model, &d, false)?;
[623](#623)        if cols.is_empty() {
[624](#624)            return Ok(());
[625](#625)        }
[626](#626)        let set: Vec<String> = cols
[627](#627)            .iter()
[628](#628)            .enumerate()
[629](#629)            .map(|(i, (c, _))| format!("{} = ${}::{}", c, i + 1, col_cast(parent_model, c)))
[630](#630)            .collect();
[631](#631)        let id_ph = cols.len() + 1;
[632](#632)        let mut params: Vec<Value> = cols.iter().map(|(_, v)| v.clone()).collect();
[633](#633)        params.push(Value::Int(pid));
[634](#634)        let mut where_sql = match record_rule_domain(Operation::Write, parent_model.name, ctx, rules) {
[635](#635)            Some(rule) => format!("id = ${id_ph} AND {}", rule.compile_into(parent_model, &mut params)?),
[636](#636)            None => format!("id = ${id_ph}"),
[637](#637)        };
[638](#638)        where_sql.push_str(&company_clause(parent_model, ctx, &mut params)?);
[639](#639)        let sql = format!("UPDATE {} SET {} WHERE {}", parent_model.table, set.join(", "), where_sql);
[640](#640)        let mut q = sqlx::query(&sql);
[641](#641)        for v in ¶ms {
[642](#642)            q = bind_query(q, v);
[643](#643)        }
[644](#644)        if q.execute(&mut **tx).await?.rows_affected() == 0 {
[645](#645)            return Err(DbError::AccessDenied {
[646](#646)                model: parent_model.name.to_string(),
[647](#647)                operation: "write (inherited parent not found or not permitted)",
[648](#648)            });
[649](#649)        }
[650](#650)        if !computed_fields(parent_model).is_empty() {
[653](#653)            sqlx::query("SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext($1)::bigint)")
[654](#654)                .bind(format!("agg:{}:{}", parent_model.table, pid))
[655](#655)                .execute(&mut **tx)
[656](#656)                .await?;
[657](#657)            recompute_columns_on(tx, parent_model, pid).await?;
[658](#658)        }
[659](#659)        Ok(())
[660](#660)    }

[662](#662)    pub async fn update_secured(
[668](#668)        &self,
[669](#669)        model: &ResolvedModel,
[670](#670)        ctx: &Ctx,
[671](#671)        acls: &[Acl],
[672](#672)        rules: &[RecordRule],
[673](#673)        id: i64,
[674](#674)        values: &Map<String, Json>,
[675](#675)    ) -> Result<u64, DbError> {
[676](#676)        let before = self.parent_targets(model, id).await?;
[680](#680)        let mut tx = self.pool.begin().await?;
[681](#681)        let (affected, track_changes) =
[682](#682)            self.update_secured_in_tx(model, ctx, acls, rules, id, values, &mut tx).await?;
[683](#683)        if affected == 0 {
[684](#684)            return Ok(0); }
[686](#686)        tx.commit().await?;
[687](#687)
[688](#688)        let after = self.parent_targets(model, id).await?;
[691](#691)        let mut seen: Vec<(&'static str, i64)> = Vec::new();
[692](#692)        for (parent, pid) in before.into_iter().chain(after) {
[693](#693)            if !seen.iter().any(|&(n, p)| n == parent.name && p == pid) {
[694](#694)                seen.push((parent.name, pid));
[695](#695)                self.recompute_parent(&parent, pid).await?;
[696](#696)            }
[697](#697)        }
[698](#698)
[699](#699)        if !track_changes.is_empty() {
[703](#703)            if let Err(e) = self.write_tracking(model.name, id, ctx.uid, &track_changes).await {
[704](#704)                eprintln!("kigumi-db tracking write failed (write committed): {e:?}");
[705](#705)            }
[706](#706)        }
[707](#707)        Ok(affected)
[708](#708)    }

[913](#913)                    change_summary: serde_json::json!({ "changed_fields": changed }),
[914](#914)                },

[920](#920)                    .into_iter()

[930](#930)                            author_uid: Some(ctx.uid),
[931](#931)                            company_id,

[933](#933)                        },
[934](#934)                    )
[935](#935)                    .await?;
[936](#936)                }
[937](#937)            }
[938](#938)        }
[939](#939)
[940](#940)        let mut track_changes: Vec<(String, Option<String>, Option<String>)> = Vec::new();

[945](#945)            let old_t = old_text.iter().find(|(k, _)| k == c).and_then(|(_, o)| o.clone());

[948](#948)                track_changes.push((c.to_string(), old_t, new_t));
[949](#949)            }
[950](#950)        }
[951](#951)        Ok((affected, track_changes))
[952](#952)    }

[1155](#1155)    pub async fn run_action(
[1160](#1160)        &self,
[1161](#1161)        model: &ResolvedModel,
[1162](#1162)        ctx: &Ctx,
[1163](#1163)        acls: &[Acl],
[1164](#1164)        rules: &[RecordRule],
[1165](#1165)        id: i64,
[1166](#1166)        action_name: &str,
[1167](#1167)    ) -> Result<(), DbError> {
[1168](#1168)        let action = action_for(model.name, action_name).ok_or_else(|| {
[1169](#1169)            DbError::BadInput(format!("unknown action '{action_name}' on '{}'", model.name))
[1170](#1170)        })?;
[1171](#1171)        if !check_access(Operation::Write, model.name, ctx, acls) {
[1172](#1172)            return Err(DbError::AccessDenied { model: model.name.to_string(), operation: "action" });
[1173](#1173)        }
[1174](#1174)        if !action.groups.is_empty() && !ctx.is_su() && !action.groups.iter().any(|g| ctx.is_member(g)) {
[1175](#1175)            return Err(DbError::AccessDenied { model: model.name.to_string(), operation: "action (group)" });
[1176](#1176)        }
[1177](#1177)        if self.find_one_secured(model, ctx, acls, rules, id).await?.is_none() {
[1179](#1179)            return Err(DbError::BadInput("record not found or not permitted".to_string()));
[1180](#1180)        }
[1181](#1181)        let mut conn = self.pool.acquire().await?;
[1182](#1182)        let record = read_record_on(&mut conn, model, id)
[1183](#1183)            .await?
[1184](#1184)            .ok_or_else(|| DbError::BadInput("record not found".to_string()))?;
[1185](#1185)        drop(conn);
[1186](#1186)
[1187](#1187)        let outcome = (action.func)(&ActionInput::new(&record)).map_err(DbError::BadInput)?;
[1188](#1188)        let mut updates: Map<String, Json> =
[1189](#1189)            outcome.set.iter().map(|(k, v)| (k.clone(), value_to_json(v))).collect();
[1190](#1190)        if let Some((field, code)) = &outcome.assign_sequence {
[1191](#1191)            updates.insert(field.clone(), Json::from(self.next_value(code).await?));
[1192](#1192)        }
[1193](#1193)        if updates.is_empty() {
[1194](#1194)            return Ok(()); }
[1196](#1196)        if self.update_secured(model, ctx, acls, rules, id, &updates).await? == 0 {
[1197](#1197)            return Err(DbError::BadInput("record not found or not permitted".to_string()));
[1198](#1198)        }
[1199](#1199)        Ok(())
[1200](#1200)    }

[1310](#1310)    async fn recompute_parent(&self, parent: &ResolvedModel, parent_id: i64) -> Result<(), DbError> {
[1316](#1316)        let mut work: Vec<(ResolvedModel, i64, usize)> = vec![(parent.clone(), parent_id, 0)];
[1320](#1320)        let mut seen: Vec<(&'static str, i64)> = Vec::new();
[1321](#1321)        while let Some((m, pid, depth)) = work.pop() {
[1322](#1322)            if depth > MAX_CASCADE_DEPTH || seen.iter().any(|&(n, i)| n == m.name && i == pid) {
[1323](#1323)                continue;
[1324](#1324)            }
[1325](#1325)            seen.push((m.name, pid));
[1326](#1326)            if computed_fields(&m).is_empty() {
[1327](#1327)                continue;
[1328](#1328)            }
[1329](#1329)            let mut lock = self.pool.begin().await?;
[1332](#1332)            sqlx::query("SELECT pg_advisory_xact_lock(hashtext($1)::bigint)")
[1333](#1333)                .bind(format!("agg:{}:{}", m.table, pid))
[1334](#1334)                .execute(&mut *lock)
[1335](#1335)                .await?;
[1336](#1336)            recompute_columns_on(&mut lock, &m, pid).await?;
[1337](#1337)            lock.commit().await?;
[1338](#1338)            for (gp, inverse) in parents_of(m.name) {
[1340](#1340)                if let Some(gpid) = self.read_fk(m.table, inverse, pid).await? {
[1341](#1341)                    work.push((gp, gpid, depth + 1));
[1342](#1342)                }
[1343](#1343)            }
[1344](#1344)        }
[1345](#1345)        Ok(())
[1346](#1346)    }

[1662](#1662)fn validate_write_values(
[1668](#1668)    model: &ResolvedModel,
[1669](#1669)    values: &Map<String, Json>,
[1670](#1670)    require_all: bool,
[1671](#1671)) -> Result<Vec<(&'static str, Value)>, DbError> {
[1672](#1672)    let mut out = Vec::new();
[1673](#1673)    for (key, jv) in values {
[1674](#1674)        let field = model
[1675](#1675)            .fields
[1676](#1676)            .iter()
[1677](#1677)            .find(|f| f.name == key)
[1678](#1678)            .ok_or_else(|| DbError::BadInput(format!("unknown field '{key}'")))?;
[1679](#1679)        if !field.has_column() {
[1680](#1680)            return Err(DbError::BadInput(format!("field '{key}' is not a stored column")));
[1681](#1681)        }
[1682](#1682)        if field.is_computed() {
[1683](#1683)            return Err(DbError::BadInput(format!("field '{key}' is computed and not writable")));
[1684](#1684)        }
[1685](#1685)        if field_is_readonly(model.name, field.name) {
[1686](#1686)            return Err(DbError::BadInput(format!("field '{key}' is read-only and not writable")));
[1687](#1687)        }
[1688](#1688)        if jv.is_null() && field.required {
[1689](#1689)            return Err(DbError::Invalid {
[1690](#1690)                message: format!("field '{key}' is required and cannot be null"),
[1691](#1691)                fields: vec![(key.clone(), "required".to_string())],
[1692](#1692)            });
[1693](#1693)        }
[1694](#1694)        out.push((field.name, json_to_value(field, jv)?));
[1695](#1695)    }
[1696](#1696)    if require_all {
[1697](#1697)        for f in &model.fields {
[1698](#1698)            if f.has_column() && !f.is_computed() && f.required && !values.contains_key(f.name) {
[1699](#1699)                return Err(DbError::Invalid {
[1700](#1700)                    message: format!("field '{}' is required", f.name),
[1701](#1701)                    fields: vec![(f.name.to_string(), "required".to_string())],
[1702](#1702)                });
[1703](#1703)            }
[1704](#1704)        }
[1705](#1705)    }
[1706](#1706)    Ok(out)

[1738](#1738)fn split_nested(
[1743](#1743)    model: &ResolvedModel,
[1744](#1744)    values: &Map<String, Json>,
[1745](#1745)) -> Result<(Map<String, Json>, Vec<NestedWrite>, Vec<M2mSet>, Map<String, Json>), DbError> {
[1746](#1746)    let mut scalars = Map::new();
[1747](#1747)    let mut nested = Vec::new();
[1748](#1748)    let mut m2m = Vec::new();
[1749](#1749)    let mut delegated = Map::new();
[1750](#1750)    let deleg_names: Vec<&'static str> =
[1752](#1752)        delegated_fields(model.name).map_err(DbError::BadInput)?.iter().map(|d| d.def.name).collect();
[1753](#1753)    for (key, jv) in values {
[1754](#1754)        match model.fields.iter().find(|f| f.name == *key).map(|f| f.kind) {
[1755](#1755)            Some(FieldKind::Many2many { relation, column, target_column, .. }) => {
[1756](#1756)                if jv.is_null() {
[1757](#1757)                    continue; }
[1759](#1759)                let arr = jv
[1760](#1760)                    .as_array()
[1761](#1761)                    .ok_or_else(|| DbError::BadInput(format!("'{key}' must be an array of ids")))?;
[1762](#1762)                let mut ids = Vec::with_capacity(arr.len());
[1763](#1763)                for v in arr {
[1764](#1764)                    ids.push(
[1765](#1765)                        v.as_i64().ok_or_else(|| DbError::BadInput(format!("'{key}': ids must be integers")))?,
[1766](#1766)                    );
[1767](#1767)                }
[1768](#1768)                m2m.push(M2mSet { relation, column, target_column, ids });
[1769](#1769)            }
[1770](#1770)            Some(FieldKind::One2many { target, inverse }) => {
[1771](#1771)                let arr = jv.as_array().ok_or_else(|| {
[1772](#1772)                    DbError::BadInput(format!("'{key}' must be an array of child commands"))
[1773](#1773)                })?;
[1774](#1774)                if arr.len() > MAX_O2M_COMMANDS {
[1775](#1775)                    return Err(DbError::BadInput(format!(
[1776](#1776)                        "'{key}': too many child commands ({}, max {MAX_O2M_COMMANDS})",
[1777](#1777)                        arr.len()
[1778](#1778)                    )));
[1779](#1779)                }
[1780](#1780)                let commands: Vec<O2mCommand> =
[1781](#1781)                    arr.iter().map(|item| parse_o2m_command(key, item)).collect::<Result<_, _>>()?;
[1782](#1782)                if !commands.is_empty() {
[1783](#1783)                    let child = resolve_registered(target).map_err(|e| {
[1784](#1784)                        DbError::BadInput(format!("unknown child model '{target}': {e}"))
[1785](#1785)                    })?;
[1786](#1786)                    nested.push(NestedWrite { child, inverse, commands });
[1787](#1787)                }
[1788](#1788)            }
[1789](#1789)            _ if deleg_names.contains(&key.as_str()) => {
[1791](#1791)                delegated.insert(key.clone(), jv.clone());
[1792](#1792)            }
[1793](#1793)            _ => {
[1795](#1795)                scalars.insert(key.clone(), jv.clone());
[1796](#1796)            }
[1797](#1797)        }
[1798](#1798)    }
[1799](#1799)    Ok((scalars, nested, m2m, delegated))

[1802](#1802)async fn apply_m2m_in_tx(
[1805](#1805)    tx: &mut sqlx::Transaction<'_, Postgres>,
[1806](#1806)    record_id: i64,

[1814](#1814)        for &tid in &s.ids {
[1815](#1815)            sqlx::query(&format!(
[1816](#1816)                "INSERT INTO {} ({}, {}) VALUES ($1, $2) ON CONFLICT DO NOTHING",
[1817](#1817)                s.relation, s.column, s.target_column
[1818](#1818)            ))
[1819](#1819)            .bind(record_id)
[1820](#1820)            .bind(tid)

[1828](#1828)fn parse_o2m_command(field: &str, item: &Json) -> Result<O2mCommand, DbError> {
[1829](#1829)    let obj = item
[1830](#1830)        .as_object()
[1831](#1831)        .ok_or_else(|| DbError::BadInput(format!("each '{field}' item must be an object")))?;
[1832](#1832)    let values = || {
[1833](#1833)        obj.get("values")
[1834](#1834)            .and_then(|v| v.as_object())
[1835](#1835)            .cloned()
[1836](#1836)            .ok_or_else(|| DbError::BadInput(format!("'{field}' command needs a 'values' object")))
[1837](#1837)    };
[1838](#1838)    let id = || {
[1839](#1839)        obj.get("id")
[1840](#1840)            .and_then(|v| v.as_i64())
[1841](#1841)            .ok_or_else(|| DbError::BadInput(format!("'{field}' command needs an integer 'id'")))
[1842](#1842)    };
[1843](#1843)    Ok(match obj.get("op").and_then(|v| v.as_str()) {
[1844](#1844)        None => {
[1845](#1845)            if obj.contains_key("id") {
[1846](#1846)                return Err(DbError::BadInput(format!(
[1847](#1847)                    "'{field}': an item with 'id' must use op 'update' or 'delete'"
[1848](#1848)                )));
[1849](#1849)            }
[1850](#1850)            O2mCommand::Create(obj.clone())
[1851](#1851)        }
[1852](#1852)        Some("create") => O2mCommand::Create(values()?),
[1853](#1853)        Some("update") => O2mCommand::Update(id()?, values()?),
[1854](#1854)        Some("delete") => O2mCommand::Delete(id()?),
[1855](#1855)        Some(other) => return Err(DbError::BadInput(format!("'{field}': unknown op '{other}'"))),
[1856](#1856)    })

[2019](#2019)fn json_to_value(field: &FieldDef, jv: &Json) -> Result<Value, DbError> {
[2020](#2020)    let bad = || {

[2037](#2037)                    field.name

[2042](#2042)        (FieldKind::Integer | FieldKind::Many2one { .. } | FieldKind::Image, Json::Number(n)) => {

[2058](#2058)        (FieldKind::Float, Json::Number(n)) => Value::Float(n.as_f64().ok_or_else(bad)?),
[2059](#2059)        (FieldKind::Float, Json::String(s)) => Value::Float(s.trim().parse().map_err(|_| bad())?),
[2061](#2061)        (FieldKind::Date | FieldKind::Datetime, Json::String(s)) => Value::Str(s.clone()),

[2217](#2217)fn parents_of(child_model_name: &str) -> Vec<(ResolvedModel, &'static str)> {
[2218](#2218)    let mut out = Vec::new();

[2232](#2232)
[2233](#2233)fn select_columns(model: &ResolvedModel) -> String {
[2234](#2234)    let mut cols = vec!["id".to_string()];
[2235](#2235)    for f in &model.fields {
[2236](#2236)        if f.has_column() {
[2237](#2237)            match f.kind {
[2238](#2238)                FieldKind::Date | FieldKind::Datetime => cols.push(format!("{0}::text AS {0}", f.name)),
[2241](#2241)                _ => cols.push(f.name.to_string()),
[2242](#2242)            }
[2243](#2243)        } else if let Some(path) = related_path(model.name, f.name) {
[2244](#2244)            if let Ok(sq) = related_subquery(model, path) {
[2246](#2246)                cols.push(format!("{sq} AS {}", f.name));
[2247](#2247)            }
[2248](#2248)        } else if let FieldKind::Many2many { relation, column, target_column, .. } = f.kind {
[2249](#2249)            cols.push(format!(
[2251](#2251)                "(SELECT COALESCE(array_agg({tc} ORDER BY {tc}), '{{}}'::bigint[]) FROM {rel} WHERE {col} = {tbl}.id) AS {name}",
[2252](#2252)                tc = target_column, rel = relation, col = column, tbl = model.table, name = f.name
[2253](#2253)            ));
[2254](#2254)        }
[2255](#2255)    }
[2256](#2256)    for d in delegated_fields(model.name).unwrap_or_default() {
[2259](#2259)        let read = match d.def.kind {
[2260](#2260)            FieldKind::Date | FieldKind::Datetime => format!("{}::text", d.def.name),
[2261](#2261)            _ => d.def.name.to_string(),
[2262](#2262)        };
[2263](#2263)        cols.push(format!(
[2264](#2264)            "(SELECT {read} FROM {ptable} WHERE id = {ctable}.{via}) AS {name}",
[2265](#2265)            ptable = d.parent_table, ctable = model.table, via = d.via, name = d.def.name
[2266](#2266)        ));
[2267](#2267)    }
[2268](#2268)    cols.join(", ")
[2269](#2269)}
[2270](#2270)
[2271](#2271)fn related_subquery(model: &ResolvedModel, path: &str) -> Result<String, DbError> {
[2275](#2275)    let segs: Vec<&str> = path.split('.').collect();
[2276](#2276)    if segs.len() < 2 {
[2277](#2277)        return Err(DbError::BadInput(format!("related path '{path}' must traverse a relation")));
[2278](#2278)    }
[2279](#2279)    let first = model
[2280](#2280)        .fields
[2281](#2281)        .iter()
[2282](#2282)        .find(|f| f.name == segs[0])
[2283](#2283)        .ok_or_else(|| DbError::BadInput(format!("related path: unknown field '{}'", segs[0])))?;
[2284](#2284)    let target = match &first.kind {
[2285](#2285)        FieldKind::Many2one { target } => target,
[2286](#2286)        _ => return Err(DbError::BadInput(format!("related path: '{}' is not a Many2one", segs[0]))),
[2287](#2287)    };
[2288](#2288)    let mut cur = resolve_registered(target).map_err(DbError::BadInput)?;
[2289](#2289)    let mut id_expr = format!("{}.{}", model.table, segs[0]);
[2290](#2290)    for (i, seg) in segs.iter().enumerate().skip(1) {
[2291](#2291)        let f = cur
[2292](#2292)            .fields
[2293](#2293)            .iter()
[2294](#2294)            .find(|f| f.name == *seg)
[2295](#2295)            .ok_or_else(|| DbError::BadInput(format!("related path: unknown field '{seg}' on '{}'", cur.name)))?;
[2296](#2296)        if i == segs.len() - 1 {
[2297](#2297)            let read = match f.kind {
[2298](#2298)                FieldKind::Date | FieldKind::Datetime => format!("{seg}::text"),
[2299](#2299)                _ => seg.to_string(),
[2300](#2300)            };
[2301](#2301)            return Ok(format!("(SELECT {read} FROM {} WHERE id = {id_expr})", cur.table));
[2302](#2302)        }
[2303](#2303)        let next = match &f.kind {
[2304](#2304)            FieldKind::Many2one { target } => target,
[2305](#2305)            _ => return Err(DbError::BadInput(format!("related path: '{seg}' is not a Many2one"))),
[2306](#2306)        };
[2307](#2307)        id_expr = format!("(SELECT {seg} FROM {} WHERE id = {id_expr})", cur.table);
[2308](#2308)        cur = resolve_registered(next).map_err(DbError::BadInput)?;
[2309](#2309)    }
[2310](#2310)    unreachable!("the loop returns on the final segment")
[2311](#2311)}
[2312](#2312)
[2313](#2313)fn decode_value(row: &PgRow, name: &str, kind: &FieldKind) -> Value {
[2316](#2316)    match kind {
[2317](#2317)        FieldKind::Text | FieldKind::Html | FieldKind::Selection(_) => {
[2318](#2318)            row.try_get::<Option<String>, _>(name).ok().flatten().map(Value::Str).unwrap_or(Value::Null)
[2319](#2319)        }
[2320](#2320)        FieldKind::Integer | FieldKind::Many2one { .. } | FieldKind::Image => {
[2321](#2321)            row.try_get::<Option<i64>, _>(name).ok().flatten().map(Value::Int).unwrap_or(Value::Null)
[2322](#2322)        }
[2323](#2323)        FieldKind::Float => {
[2324](#2324)            row.try_get::<Option<f64>, _>(name).ok().flatten().map(Value::Float).unwrap_or(Value::Null)
[2325](#2325)        }
[2326](#2326)        FieldKind::Decimal { .. } => row
[2327](#2327)            .try_get::<Option<rust_decimal::Decimal>, _>(name)
[2328](#2328)            .ok()
[2329](#2329)            .flatten()
[2330](#2330)            .map(Value::Decimal)
[2331](#2331)            .unwrap_or(Value::Null),
[2332](#2332)        FieldKind::Bool => {
[2333](#2333)            row.try_get::<Option<bool>, _>(name).ok().flatten().map(Value::Bool).unwrap_or(Value::Null)
[2334](#2334)        }
[2335](#2335)        FieldKind::Date | FieldKind::Datetime => {
[2337](#2337)            row.try_get::<Option<String>, _>(name).ok().flatten().map(Value::Str).unwrap_or(Value::Null)
[2338](#2338)        }
[2339](#2339)        FieldKind::Many2many { .. } => Value::List(
[2341](#2341)            row.try_get::<Option<Vec<i64>>, _>(name)
[2342](#2342)                .ok()
[2343](#2343)                .flatten()
[2344](#2344)                .unwrap_or_default()

[2383](#2383)        FieldKind::Decimal { .. } => match row.try_get::<Option<rust_decimal::Decimal>, _>(name)? {

[2391](#2391)        FieldKind::Many2many { .. } => {
[2392](#2392)            let ids: Vec<i64> = row.try_get::<Option<Vec<i64>>, _>(name)?.unwrap_or_default();

[2443](#2443)fn filter_path_accessible(model: &ResolvedModel, path: &str, ctx: &Ctx) -> bool {
[2449](#2449)    if ctx.is_su() {
[2450](#2450)        return true;
[2451](#2451)    }
[2452](#2452)    let mut cur: ResolvedModel = model.clone();
[2453](#2453)    let mut segs = path.split('.').peekable();
[2454](#2454)    while let Some(seg) = segs.next() {
[2455](#2455)        if !field_accessible(cur.name, seg, ctx) {
[2456](#2456)            return false;
[2457](#2457)        }
[2458](#2458)        if segs.peek().is_none() {
[2459](#2459)            break; }
[2461](#2461)        match cur.fields.iter().find(|f| f.name == seg).map(|f| &f.kind) {
[2463](#2463)            Some(FieldKind::Many2one { target }) | Some(FieldKind::One2many { target, .. }) => {
[2464](#2464)                match resolve_registered(target) {
[2465](#2465)                    Ok(m) => cur = m,
[2466](#2466)                    Err(_) => return true,
[2468](#2468)                }
[2469](#2469)            }
[2470](#2470)            _ => return true,
[2472](#2472)        }
[2473](#2473)    }
[2474](#2474)    true

# Db in kigumi_db - Rust

`pub struct Db { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

A connection pool to a Postgres database. `Clone` shares the same pool (cheap; `PgPool` is an
`Arc` internally) — e.g. to hand a handle to the background cron scheduler.

and whose domain is parsed into a `RuleDomain::Owned`. Call ONCE at startup; the result is
appended to the static (compiled-in) rules — both flow through the same engine, so a DB rule
adds to (never silently removes) the static baseline (global rules AND, group rules OR).

#### pub async fn [revoke_refresh](https://docs.rs#method.revoke_refresh)(&self, jti: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [DbError](https://docs.rs/enum.DbError.html)>

Atomically claims (revokes) an active refresh token, returning its user id. The check and
the revoke happen in ONE statement, so two concurrent claims of the same token cannot both
succeed: the loser’s UPDATE affects zero rows → `None`. This prevents refresh double-spend.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/kigumi_db/cron.rs.html#68-92)#### pub async fn [run_due_crons](https://docs.rs#method.run_due_crons)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[usize](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.usize.html), [DbError](https://docs.rs/enum.DbError.html)>

Claims every due job atomically — advancing its `next_run`, with `SKIP LOCKED` so a second
scheduler can’t claim the same row — then runs each body. A failure is logged (the job retries
next interval). A persisted job with no registered body is deactivated. Returns how many ran.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/kigumi_db/cron.rs.html#121-133)#### pub async fn [ensure_transient_defaults](https://docs.rs#method.ensure_transient_defaults)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [DbError](https://docs.rs/enum.DbError.html)>

#### pub async fn [ensure_transient_defaults](https://docs.rs#method.ensure_transient_defaults)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [DbError](https://docs.rs/enum.DbError.html)>

Gives every transient model’s `create_date` a `DEFAULT now()` (idempotent; `to_ddl` emits no
column default). Postgres then stamps `create_date` on EVERY insert path, so the GC cron can
reclaim rows by age regardless of how they were created. Tolerates an unmigrated table or a
model lacking `create_date`. Run during migrate, after the tables exist.

#### pub async fn [sweep_transient_records](https://docs.rs#method.sweep_transient_records)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [DbError](https://docs.rs/enum.DbError.html)>

Reclaims ephemeral transient (wizard) rows older than the TTL, bounding their tables. Public so

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/kigumi_db/event_schema.rs.html#431-458)#### pub async fn [events_after](https://docs.rs#method.events_after)(
    &self,

) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[StoredEvent](https://docs.rs/struct.StoredEvent.html)>, [DbError](https://docs.rs/enum.DbError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/kigumi_db/event_schema.rs.html#431-458)

#### pub async fn [events_after](https://docs.rs#method.events_after)(
    &self,
    cursor: ([i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html), [i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html)),
    limit: [i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[StoredEvent](https://docs.rs/struct.StoredEvent.html)>, [DbError](https://docs.rs/enum.DbError.html)>

Events after the `(txn, id)` cursor, GAP-SAFE. Two properties compose: (1) only rows whose
writer transaction is below every RUNNING transaction are eligible (`tx_id < pg_snapshot_xmin(pg_current_snapshot())`) — the eligible set is stable and only ever grows;
(2) it grows in (txn, id) order, so a (txn, id) cursor can never skip. An id-only cursor is
NOT safe: a long transaction carries the xid of its FIRST write but inserts events late with
HIGH ids — an overlapping younger writer’s lower id would fall behind the cursor forever.
The trade-off is delivery lag bounded by the longest concurrent write transaction.
Pre-migration rows (tx_id NULL) read as txn 0 — a legacy prefix.

    &self,
    ctx: &[Ctx](https://docs.rs/kigumi-core/0.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/kigumi_core/security/struct.Ctx.html),
    acls: &[[Acl](https://docs.rs/kigumi-core/0.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/kigumi_core/security/struct.Acl.html)],
    rules: &[[RecordRule](https://docs.rs/kigumi-core/0.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/kigumi_core/security/struct.RecordRule.html)],
    events: &[[StoredEvent](https://docs.rs/struct.StoredEvent.html)],

Filters a batch of events down to what `ctx` may SEE, and shapes each into the stream JSON.
Read ACL first (in memory); then each live-record event re-reads its row through
`find_one_secured` — THE visibility path every read uses (record rules + company scope) —
memoized per (model, record) within the batch. (`id` is not domain-addressable today, so a
batched id-IN secured query is not expressible; batches are small — one poll tick.)
`model.deleted` events cannot re-read the row, so they gate on the Read ACL, the event’s
company against the caller’s scope (NULL = shared = visible; default-deny otherwise, like
`company_filter`) — AND are suppressed entirely when a Read record rule applies to this
caller on the model (the rule cannot be evaluated against a gone row; default-deny, matching
the posture everywhere else). `changed_fields` names are filtered per field ACL (D6), and a
`model.state_changed` whose `state` field is D6-restricted for this caller has its
field/from/to values blanked — record visibility must not leak restricted VALUES. Custom
service events (`ServiceCtx::emit_event`) pass their summary through: it is visible to every
caller who can see the record (documented on emit_event).

Additive in-place column sync: for each of `model`’s fields that has an own column but is missing
from the live table, add it via `ALTER TABLE ... ADD COLUMN IF NOT EXISTS`. ADDITIVE ONLY — it
never drops, renames, retypes, or adds NOT NULL / UNIQUE / CHECK / DEFAULT to an existing table
(those can fail or lock a populated table; required-ness is enforced at the write layer, and the
new column is simply NULL on existing rows). This is the safety net that materializes a newly
added `#[field]` on an already-installed table without a DB reset; run on migrate after the
model/install pass. Idempotent (IF NOT EXISTS) and race-safe, like the custom-field ALTER.

#### pub async fn [is_module_installed](https://docs.rs#method.is_module_installed)(&self, name: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), [DbError](https://docs.rs/enum.DbError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/kigumi_db/module_store.rs.html#92-105)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/kigumi_db/module_store.rs.html#92-105)

Records a module as installed (or updates its recorded version). Migrating its tables is the
caller’s job. RE-installing a previously-uninstalled module keeps the OLD recorded version:
its tables kept their old-shape data, so the next migrate must replay the pending
`register_migration!` steps from where that data really is — recording the linked version
here would skip them silently (review must-fix).

Removes a module from the installed set. Its tables and data are left untouched (disable, not drop) and the ledger row is kept flagged — NOT deleted — so a later re-install still knows what version the kept data is at and replays the data migrations it missed.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/kigumi_db/module_store.rs.html#124-151)#### pub async fn [migrate_installed_schema](https://docs.rs#method.migrate_installed_schema)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [DbError](https://docs.rs/enum.DbError.html)>

#### pub async fn [migrate_installed_schema](https://docs.rs#method.migrate_installed_schema)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [DbError](https://docs.rs/enum.DbError.html)>

Migrates the SCHEMA of every currently-installed module (the model tables in FK-dependency
order, then Many2many junctions, then the framework indexes and the cron ledger). Idempotent —
re-running at the same version is a no-op. This is the reusable core of the CLI’s
`migrate_installed`; the CLI then layers module reference-data seeding on top. The server calls
it on a live install so a newly-installed module’s tables exist without a restart. Reference-data
seeds are NOT run here (they live with the host).

Runs every pending `register_migration!` step: for each installed module whose linked crate
is NEWER than the ledger version, applies the registered migrations with
`ledger < to_version <= linked` in semver order, bumping the ledger after each step (a
failure resumes from the failed step on the next migrate). Modules with a version bump but
no registered steps just get their ledger bumped. A linked version OLDER than the ledger is
a refused downgrade. Returns the applied `(module, to_version)` steps.

Claims a batch of due jobs (atomically: `pending` → `running` + lease, `FOR UPDATE SKIP LOCKED` so concurrent workers never double-claim) and runs each. Success → `done`; failure →
exponential backoff, or `dead` at the registration’s `max_attempts`; an UNREGISTERED name
(a stale row from a removed job) → `dead` with a clear error. Returns how many ran.

Pins `DateStyle = ISO, YMD` on every pooled connection: the codebase renders dates/datetimes
as `::text` and assumes ISO `YYYY-MM-DD` (big-endian, so lexical order == chronological) — for
activity-state derivation, tracking diffs, and the frontend’s date parsing. A server/role
default of `SQL`/`Postgres`/`German` would otherwise silently break those; don’t inherit it.

Lightweight reachability check for readiness probes.

#### pub async fn [run_action](https://docs.rs#method.run_action)(
    &self,
    model: &[ResolvedModel](https://docs.rs/kigumi-core/0.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/kigumi_core/metamodel/struct.ResolvedModel.html),
    ctx: &[Ctx](https://docs.rs/kigumi-core/0.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/kigumi_core/security/struct.Ctx.html),
    acls: &[[Acl](https://docs.rs/kigumi-core/0.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/kigumi_core/security/struct.Acl.html)],
    rules: &[[RecordRule](https://docs.rs/kigumi-core/0.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/kigumi_core/security/struct.RecordRule.html)],
    id: [i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html),
    action_name: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [DbError](https://docs.rs/enum.DbError.html)>

Runs a registered state-transition action on row `id`: enforces ACL Write + the action’s group
guard + record-rule visibility, runs the pure action fn over the current record, resolves any
sequence assignment (gapless numbering), and applies the resulting updates through the secured
write path (so record rules + company scope are re-checked on the write).

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/kigumi_db/lib.rs.html#1264-1308)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/kigumi_db/lib.rs.html#1264-1308)

Flushes the outgoing mail queue: hands every `mail.mail` in state `outgoing` to `send` (the host’s
SMTP transport) and marks each `sent` or `exception` (recording the error). The transport stays at
the app level (lettre), so this crate has no mail dependency — `send` is a synchronous closure
(use a blocking SMTP transport). Tolerates an unmigrated `mail_mail` (mail not installed). Returns
the number successfully sent.

Deletes row `id`, enforcing ACL Delete and the Delete record rule. Returns rows deleted.

The database clock as an ISO-8601 string, for stamping mail messages/tracking/activities. One clock (the DB) for every mail row, so ordering is consistent regardless of caller.

The database’s current date as `YYYY-MM-DD`, for deriving an activity’s state (overdue/today/
planned) by lexical comparison against its ISO `date_deadline`. One clock = one source of truth.

The tracking rows for the given message ids, as JSON `{message_id, field, old_value, new_value}` (ordered). Tolerates an unmigrated `mail_tracking`. For embedding audit entries
into a thread read.

#### pub async fn [ensure_mail_indexes](https://docs.rs#method.ensure_mail_indexes)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [DbError](https://docs.rs/enum.DbError.html)>

Creates the mail subsystem’s lookup indexes (idempotent, tolerant of unmigrated tables): the
polymorphic `mail_message(res_model, res_id)` thread lookup and `mail_tracking(message_id)`.
The metamodel can’t express indexes yet and the mail tables are a known framework concern, so
the framework ensures them directly — like the sequence schema. Run during migrate.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/kigumi_db/lib.rs.html#1612-1624)#### pub async fn [ensure_stock_indexes](https://docs.rs#method.ensure_stock_indexes)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [DbError](https://docs.rs/enum.DbError.html)>

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/kigumi_db/lib.rs.html#1612-1624)

#### pub async fn [ensure_stock_indexes](https://docs.rs#method.ensure_stock_indexes)(&self) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[()](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.unit.html), [DbError](https://docs.rs/enum.DbError.html)>

Stock indexes: one quant per (product, location, lot) — a composite UNIQUE the metamodel can’t
express, and the anchor for the `ON CONFLICT (product_id, location_id, COALESCE(lot_id, 0))` upsert
the move-done mechanism uses. `COALESCE(lot_id, 0)` collapses untracked bulk (NULL lot) into a
single row per (product, location), so legacy/untracked stock stays one quant. The new index is
created BEFORE the old single-key one is dropped, so a quant is always uniquely constrained.
Tolerates an unmigrated `stock_quant` (the stock module isn’t installed). Run during migrate.

pub struct RouteInput {

```
[Ctx](https://docs.rs/kigumi-core/0.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/kigumi_core/security/struct.Ctx.html),
    pub query: [Map](https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0.150/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_json/map/struct.Map.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html), [Value](https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0.150/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_json/value/enum.Value.html)>,
    pub body: [Map](https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0.150/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_json/map/struct.Map.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html), [Value](https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0.150/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_json/value/enum.Value.html)>,
    pub raw_body: [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)>,
    pub headers: [BTreeMap](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/collections/btree/map/struct.BTreeMap.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html), [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
}## Expand description

Everything a module route body receives, expressed in DB/JSON terms (no axum types):
the caller context (authenticated, or the GUEST context for `auth: false` routes), the query
params, the parsed JSON body (empty when the body is not a JSON object — NOT an error: webhook
senders post forms and raw payloads), the EXACT raw bytes (HMAC signature verification must hash
what was sent, not a re-serialization), and the request headers (lowercased names, duplicate
values joined with “, “).

### impl [RouteInput](https://docs.rs/struct.RouteInput.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/kigumi_db/service.rs.html#157-163)#### pub fn [verify_hmac_sha256](https://docs.rs#method.verify_hmac_sha256)(&self, secret: &[[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)], signature_hex: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/kigumi_db/service.rs.html#157-163)

#### pub fn [verify_hmac_sha256](https://docs.rs#method.verify_hmac_sha256)(&self, secret: &[[u8](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u8.html)], signature_hex: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)) -> [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html)

Verifies a hex-encoded HMAC-SHA256 of `raw_body` in CONSTANT TIME — the safe default for a
webhook receiver. Use THIS (or your provider’s exact scheme) rather than hand-rolling: a
plain hash of secret+body is length-extension forgeable, and a `==` comparison is a timing
oracle. Returns false on any malformed input.

# RouteRegistration in kigumi_db - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/kigumi-db/0.1.0/kigumi_db/struct.RouteRegistration.html

```
pub struct RouteRegistration {
    pub name: &'static
```
[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    pub method: [RouteMethod](https://docs.rs/enum.RouteMethod.html),
    pub auth: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
    pub groups: &'static [&'static [str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html)],
    pub func: [RouteFn](https://docs.rs/type.RouteFn.html),
}## Expand description

Registration of a module HTTP route, emitted by `register_route!`. Keyed by (name, method) — a
provider like Meta uses GET for its verification handshake and POST for delivery on the SAME
path. `auth: true` routes require a bearer (plus the optional group gate); `auth: false` routes
run under the GUEST context — uid −1, NO groups, non-su — which the default-deny ACL engine
blocks from every secured read/write, so the body must authenticate the caller itself (e.g. an
HMAC signature over `raw_body`) and then elevate explicitly via `Ctx::sudo` (the same greppable
idiom as `ServiceCtx::elevated`).

# ServiceCtx in kigumi_db - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/kigumi-db/0.1.0/kigumi_db/struct.ServiceCtx.html

`pub struct ServiceCtx<'a, 't> { /* private fields */ }`## Expand description

The secured-primitive surface handed to a service body. A concrete struct (no trait, no `dyn`): its
methods are `async fn`s delegating to `Db`’s secured CRUD under the caller’s context, so the security
engine is re-applied on every call. The ERP model-name literals a body resolves live in the MODULE,
never in this crate.

## Implementations[§](https://docs.rs#implementations)

#### pub fn [tx](https://docs.rs#method.tx)(&mut self) -> &mut [Transaction](https://docs.rs/sqlx-core/0.8.6/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sqlx_core/transaction/struct.Transaction.html)<'t, [Postgres](https://docs.rs/sqlx-postgres/0.8.6/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/sqlx_postgres/database/struct.Postgres.html)>

The LIVE service transaction, for a body that needs single-transaction atomicity (FOR UPDATE locking, a compare-and-set, multi-row updates that must commit together) — e.g. stock reservation / validation. run_service opens it, the body runs all its tx-bound SQL here, and run_service commits on Ok (rolls back on Err). Pool-based services (the secured-CRUD methods) leave it untouched.

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/kigumi_db/service.rs.html#318-333)

[Source](https://docs.rs/src/kigumi_db/service.rs.html#318-333)

Emits a domain event on the SERVICE transaction — atomic with the body’s writes (a rolled-back
service emits nothing). For a tx-bound service whose event is part of its atomic effect, e.g.
`stock.picking.done` when a transfer is validated. author_uid is the caller.

VISIBILITY: the change summary is delivered (webhooks, the live event stream) to every caller who can SEE the record — put metadata in it (ids, counts, a document number), never values of D6-restricted fields.

Enqueues a background job ON the service transaction: the job exists if and only if this service’s writes commit — the transactional-enqueue guarantee an external queue cannot give. The name must be registered via register_job! (a typo fails here, not as a dead letter).

Queues a secured insert to run AFTER the body’s tx commits (each on its own transaction, in order). For a follow-on record whose failure must NOT roll back the main effect — e.g. a stock backorder: the validation stays durable even if the backorder can’t be created (documented non-atomicity).

Explicit, greppable elevation past the gate for engine-owned rows (GL lines, join rows, sequences).

Resolve a model the service owns — the ERP model-name literal lives in the MODULE body, never here.

#### pub async fn [guarded_cas](https://docs.rs#method.guarded_cas)(
    &mut self,
    model: &[ResolvedModel](https://docs.rs/kigumi-core/0.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/kigumi_core/metamodel/struct.ResolvedModel.html),
    id: [i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html),
    set_clause: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
    extra_where: &[str](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.str.html),
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html), [DbError](https://docs.rs/enum.DbError.html)>

A guarded compare-and-set under the CALLER’s row-level authorization (Write record rule + company):
`UPDATE model SET set_clause WHERE id AND extra_where`. Static fragments only (no injection surface).
Returns true iff this call won the transition — e.g. atomically claiming an order for invoicing.
Runs on the LIVE service transaction, so the claim commits (or rolls back) WITH the body’s other
writes: a failure after the claim un-claims. A concurrent claimant’s UPDATE blocks on the row lock
until this tx resolves, then re-evaluates its guard — exactly one caller wins either way.

#### pub async fn [update_in_tx](https://docs.rs#method.update_in_tx)(
    &mut self,
    m: &[ResolvedModel](https://docs.rs/kigumi-core/0.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/kigumi_core/metamodel/struct.ResolvedModel.html),
    ctx: &[Ctx](https://docs.rs/kigumi-core/0.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/kigumi_core/security/struct.Ctx.html),
    id: [i64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.i64.html),
    values: &[Map](https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0.150/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_json/map/struct.Map.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html), [Json](https://docs.rs/serde_json/1.0.150/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/serde_json/value/enum.Value.html)>,
) -> [Result](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/result/enum.Result.html)<[u64](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.u64.html), [DbError](https://docs.rs/enum.DbError.html)>

A secured update on the LIVE service transaction (not its own) — the in-tx twin of `update_secured`,
for a write that must commit atomically with the body’s other effects (e.g. posting flips a move’s
state in the same tx that created it). The full secured path (ACL Write + D6 + record rule/company +
recompute + constraints + write triggers + domain events) runs in-tx; the tracked-field diff is
queued and written to the chatter after run_service commits (best-effort), matching `update_secured`.
Like `insert_in_tx`, it does NOT run the pool wrapper’s post-commit parent re-parenting/recompute —
use it where the updated model has no aggregate parent to roll up (e.g. account.move), or roll the
parent up yourself.

The connection pool, for a module’s own bespoke SQL the domain-based secured finds cannot express: reference reads (currency, fiscal positions, recursive category trees), junction reads, most- specific-rule queries, and engine-owned BULK operations (e.g. replacing a line’s tax breakdown rows with a single DELETE). Past the gate the body is trusted first-party code, exactly as the ERP methods were before relocation. Per-RECORD user-data writes should still go through the secured helpers so ACL/record-rule/company scope are re-applied; the raw pool is for engine-owned rows.

A secured insert on the LIVE service transaction (not its own), returning the new id — the in-tx
twin of `insert_secured`. For a service that builds a batch of related rows which must commit
atomically together, e.g. the variant generator inserting each variant plus its join rows under one
per-template advisory lock. Like the pre-relocation engine’s own `insert_secured_in_tx` use, it does
NOT run the post-commit grandparent recompute (the caller owns the tx); use it where the inserted
model has no aggregate parent to roll up.

Registration of a service by (model, name) — the transactional twin of `ActionRegistration`.

# ViewOverride in kigumi_db - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/kigumi-db/0.1.0/kigumi_db/struct.ViewOverride.html

```
pub struct ViewOverride {
    pub model:
```
[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    pub field: [String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html),
    pub label: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
    pub widget: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
    pub invisible: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
    pub readonly: [bool](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/std/primitive.bool.html),
    pub invisible_when: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
    pub readonly_when: [Option](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/core/option/enum.Option.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>,
}## Expand description

A runtime UI override for one field. `label`/`widget` replace the contract value when set; `invisible`
drops the field from the served contract; `readonly` locks it; `invisible_when`/`readonly_when` carry
a JSON domain AST for conditional visibility/lock. All fields are data — none reaches DDL.

### AccessDenied

The context is not allowed to perform the operation on the model (ACL denied).

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Migration)

### Migration([String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html))

A migration problem (e.g. an unparseable version).

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.BadInput)

### BadInput([String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html))

Invalid write input (unknown/non-writable field, or a value incompatible with its kind).

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Invalid)

### Invalid

A VALIDATION failure attributable to specific fields — the structured sibling of `BadInput`
(same HTTP 400), carrying `(field, message)` pairs a form can render inline. Produced by
`@api.constrains` violations (the rule’s declared trigger fields) and not-null rejections
(the missing column). `fields` may be empty when the rule is whole-record.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Conflict)

### Conflict([String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html))

A constraint conflict (unique violation, FK violation) — maps to HTTP 409.

    UpToDate,
}## Variants[§](https://docs.rs#variants)

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Installed)

### Installed

Fresh install: the table was created from the current model and the version recorded.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.Upgraded)

### Upgraded

Upgraded from `from` to `to` by running `steps` migration steps.

[§](https://docs.rs#variant.UpToDate)

### UpToDate

Already at (or above) the target version: nothing to do.

```
pub enum RouteMethod {
    Get,
    Post,
}
```
## Expand description

HTTP method of a module route. An enum here (not an http-crate type) keeps this crate HTTP-free; the server translates. Get also serves HEAD (axum’s default).

# m2m_junction_ddl in kigumi_db - Rust

Source: https://docs.rs/kigumi-db/0.1.0/kigumi_db/fn.m2m_junction_ddl.html

`pub fn m2m_junction_ddl(model: &`[ResolvedModel](https://docs.rs/kigumi-core/0.1.0/x86_64-unknown-linux-gnu/kigumi_core/metamodel/struct.ResolvedModel.html)) -> [Vec](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/vec/struct.Vec.html)<[String](https://doc.rust-lang.org/nightly/alloc/string/struct.String.html)>## Expand description

Builds the SELECT column list for a model. NUMERIC columns are cast to float8 so they decode
into `f64` without a decimal dependency. Identifiers come from the model, never user input.
Registered models that have a One2many field targeting `child_model_name`, paired with the
inverse FK column — i.e. the aggregate parents to recompute when such a child changes.
The exact junction-table DDL for a model’s Many2many fields — the single source shared by
[ Db::create_m2m_relations](https://docs.rs/struct.Db.html#method.create_m2m_relations) and by kigumi-test’s schema fingerprint (a template change here must
change the fingerprint verbatim, or a stale junction would survive an IF NOT EXISTS re-run).

---
